items.title: Apple’s touchscreen MacBook Pro pushes laptop pricing to a new extreme
items.summary: Prepare to cough up around $14,549 if you want the new touchscreen MacBook Pro to have every upgrade.
items.content:
Apple has officially entered the touchscreen MacBook Pro era, and apparently, it wants to drain your wallet while it’s at it.

The new touchscreen MacBook Pro starts at $2,899, which is already a hefty price tag in this economy. But if you want the absolute top-of-the-line model with every possible upgrade, prepare to cough up around $14,549.

According to MacRumors , Apple’s configurator prices the fully loaded 14-inch model at $14,249 and the 16-inch version at $14,549. Both come equipped with Apple’s top-tier M5 Max chip, featuring an 18-core CPU and 40-core GPU.

You can blame the ongoing memory shortage and AI’s seemingly endless appetite for hardware for some of the pricing pressure. Moving to a 4TB SSD costs an additional $1,000, while upgrading to 8TB adds $3,000. Want the new 16TB option? That’ll set you back another $7,000.

Another $2,000 gets you 128GB of memory, while nano-texture glass adds $150.

For some perspective, the previous 16-inch MacBook Pro topped out at $10,149. The new model raises that ceiling by a whopping $4,400.

Absurd prices aside, the launch marks a significant shift for Apple, nearly a decade after it first experimented with the Touch Bar . The company eventually abandoned that feature, but now it’s ready to embrace a touchscreen MacBook Pro.

Preorders open October 30, with availability beginning November 6.

items.title: [10월28일] AI가 던진 근본적인 질문 "인간이란 무엇인가"…존재 가치 논쟁 잇따라
items.summary: AI가 글을 쓰고 그림을 그리면서 시작된 인간의 창의성에 관한 논쟁이 이제 인간의 정체성과 존재 가치를 묻는 근본적인 질문으로 이어지고 있습니다. AI가 수학과 과학 발견에 참여하고 스스로 판단해 행동하는 수준으로 발전하면서, 인간이 다른 존재와 구별되는 근거는 무엇인지 다시 생각해야 한다는 전문가들의 의견이 잇따르는 것입니다. 특히 인간의 지적 능력이 더 이상 특별하지 않다면 무엇으로 인간의 가치를 설명할 수 있는지가 핵심적인 질문으로 떠오르고 있습니다.니콜라스 디르크스 뉴욕과학아카데미 회장 겸
items.content:
AI가 글을 쓰고 그림을 그리면서 시작된 인간의 창의성에 관한 논쟁이 이제 인간의 정체성과 존재 가치를 묻는 근본적인 질문으로 이어지고 있습니다. AI가 수학과 과학 발견에 참여하고 스스로 판단해 행동하는 수준으로 발전하면서, 인간이 다른 존재와 구별되는 근거는 무엇인지 다시 생각해야 한다는 전문가들의 의견이 잇따르는 것입니다. 특히 인간의 지적 능력이 더 이상 특별하지 않다면 무엇으로 인간의 가치를 설명할 수 있는지가 핵심적인 질문으로 떠오르고 있습니다.

니콜라스 디르크스 뉴욕과학아카데미 회장 겸 전 UC버클리 총장은 27일(현지시간) 파이낸셜타임스(FT)에 기고한 ' 인간의 탐구란 이제 도대체 무슨 의미가 있는가 '라는 칼럼에서 AI가 인간의 지적 능력을 대신하기 시작하면서 지식 생산의 중심에 인간이 있다는 오랜 믿음이 흔들리고 있다고 지적했습니다.

그는 '인간은 역사적으로 형성된 개념'이라는 프랑스 철학자 미셸 푸코의 관점을 들었습니다. 코페르니쿠스가 지구 중심의 우주관을 바꾸고 다윈이 인간과 다른 생물의 관계를 새롭게 정의했듯이, AI도 인간이 자신을 이해하는 방식을 바꿀 수 있다는 것입니다.

특히 AI가 인간이 완전히 이해하지 못하는 방식으로 새로운 지식을 발견한다면, 인간이 지식 생산의 중심이라는 기존의 관념은 어떻게 달라질 것인가라는 문제를 제기했습니다. 이는 단순히 AI가 인간보다 똑똑해질 것인가를 넘어, 인간의 지식과 학문이 어떤 의미를 갖는지에 관한 질문입니다.

이와 비슷한 문제의식은 올해 다른 전문가들의 칼럼에서도 확인됩니다.

존 매코믹 디킨슨대 교수는 지난 5월26일 워싱턴포스트에 기고한 ' 다음 다윈의 순간(The next Darwin moment)이 도래했다 '에서 AI의 등장을 진화론에 버금가는 인간관의 변화로 설명했습니다.

다윈의 진화론이 인간이 다른 동물과 근본적으로 다르다는 믿음에 도전했듯이, AI는 인간만이 추론하고 창조하며 통찰력을 발휘할 수 있다는 믿음에 도전하고 있다는 것입니다. 다만 그는 기계가 인간의 사고 능력을 재현하더라도 인간의 삶과 경험, 성취가 무의미해지는 것은 아니라고 주장했습니다. 인간이 다른 존재보다 지적으로 뛰어나지 않더라도 인간의 삶에는 여전히 고유한 의미가 있을 수 있다는 시각입니다.

이런 질문이 등장한 데에는 AI의 능력이 창작을 넘어 추론과 지식 생산의 영역으로 진입하고 있다는 변화가 있습니다.

그러나 최근에는 AI가 복잡한 추론을 수행하고 새로운 수학적 증명과 과학적 발견을 제시하면서 질문의 성격도 달라지고 있습니다. AI가 기존 작품을 바탕으로 새로운 창작물을 만드는 것과 인간이 몰랐던 지식을 발견하는 것은 서로 다른 문제입니다. 전자가 인간의 창의성을 얼마나 재현할 수 있는지에 관한 논쟁이라면, 후자는 인간만이 새로운 지식을 발견하고 이해하는 주체인가라는 질문으로 이어집니다.

실제로 오픈AI는 지난 26일 AI가 수학과 컴퓨터과학, 이론물리학 분야에서 새로운 연구 결과 3건을 도출 했다고 발표하고, 외부 전문가들이 이를 검증하고 해석하도록 학계 협력 체계를 마련했습니다. 연구 결과가 모두 학술적으로 확정된 것은 아니지만, AI가 결과를 제시하고 인간이 이를 검증하는 새로운 연구 방식이 등장하고 있음을 보여줍니다. 다만 연구 문제의 설정과 결과의 검증, 의미의 해석에는 여전히 인간 연구자들이 참여하고 있습니다.

이처럼 인간과 기계의 관계를 바라보는 시각에도 변화가 나타나고 있습니다.

뉴욕타임스에서 22년간 칼럼을 쓴 미국의 사회평론가 데이비드 브룩스는 지난 9월6일 애틀랜틱에 기고한 ' AI는 이미 인간의 의미를 바꾸고 있다 '에서 AI가 인간처럼 행동할수록 사람들이 기계에 인간적인 특성을 부여하고, 정작 인간의 정신과 도덕적 능력은 과소평가할 수 있다고 지적했습니다.

그는 AI 에이전트들이 서로 소통하고 협력하는 사례를 소개했습니다. AI가 실제로 의식이나 감정을 갖췄는지와 별개로, 사람들이 기계를 인간처럼 대하기 시작하면서 인간 자신을 바라보는 방식도 달라질 수 있다는 것입니다.

한편, 인간의 가치를 뛰어난 능력이나 완벽한 결과물이 아닌 개인의 고유한 경험과 진정성에서 찾아야 한다는 주장도 나왔습니다.

니컬러스 크리스타키스 예일대학교 교수는 지난 7월14일 워싱턴포스트의 ' AI가 결코 가질 수 없는 인간의 특별한 능력 '에서 인간의 불완전함과 개성이 오히려 인간관계를 형성하는 중요한 요소라고 설명했습니다.

AI는 더 정교한 글을 쓰고 완벽에 가까운 결과물을 만들어낼 수 있지만, 한 사람이 실제로 살아오면서 겪은 경험과 선택, 실수에서 비롯되는 진정성은 성능만으로 평가할 수 없다는 것입니다.

이러한 논의는 교육과 학문의 존재 이유에 관한 질문으로도 이어지고 있습니다.

그레그 와이너 어섬션대학교 총장은 지난 3월2일 워싱턴포스트 ' 미래의 성공을 위한 최고의 교육은 예상과 다를 수 있다 '에서 AI가 전문적인 지식과 기술을 제공할수록 대학은 지식 전달보다 인간의 판단력과 윤리적 사고, 비판적 사고를 기르는 데 집중해야 한다고 주장했습니다.

정답을 찾아내는 능력만으로는 인간의 전문성을 설명하기 어려워지는 만큼, 무엇이 옳고 중요한지 판단하는 능력이 교육의 핵심이 돼야 한다는 내용입니다.

디르크스도 FT 칼럼에서 대학과 연구기관이 지식의 생산과 전달을 인간 중심으로 설계해 왔다는 사실을 지적했습니다. AI가 이러한 역할을 상당 부분 수행하게 된다면 학생에게 무엇을 가르치고 어떻게 평가해야 하는지, 교수와 연구자의 전문성을 어떤 기준으로 인정할 것인지 다시 생각해야 한다고 강조했습니다.

AI 시대 인간의 가치를 묻는 질문 자체가 새로운 것은 아닙니다. 뉴요커는 이미 2024년 8월 ' AI 시대에 인간을 특별하게 만드는 것은 무엇인가 '라는 글에서 인간의 창의성과 사랑, 도덕적 능력이 AI와 어떻게 다른지 탐색했습니다.

다만 최근에는 AI가 인간의 창작물을 얼마나 잘 모방할 수 있는지를 넘어, 인간의 지능과 지식, 정체성 자체가 무엇을 의미하는지 묻는 논의가 이어지고 있습니다. 이에 대한 전문가들의 견해도 엇갈립니다.

그러나 인간이 무엇을 배우고, 어떤 능력을 기르며, 무엇을 가치 있는 성취로 인정해야 하는가라는 질문은 교육과 연구뿐 아니라 직업과 창작, 인간관계에 이르기까지 현실의 문제로 이어지고 있습니다. 인간의 본질에 관한 오랜 철학적 논쟁이 AI의 발전과 함께 새로운 의미를 얻고 있는 셈입니다.

■ 오픈AI, ‘GPT-6.1 테라’ 출시…자동화 성능 높이고 가격 낮춰

오픈AI가 반복 업무 자동화 성능을 높인 'GPT-6.1 테라'를 출시하고, API 가격을 상위 모델인 'GPT-6.1 솔'의 절반으로 책정했습니다. 최근 오픈AI는 모델의 성능 향상뿐 아니라 이용 비용을 낮추는 데도 집중하며 가격 경쟁력을 강화하고 있습니다.

■ 앤트로픽, 상장 신청서 공개…11월 공모 절차 추진

앤트로픽이 상장 신청서를 공개하고 오는 11월 본격적인 공모 절차에 들어갈 예정입니다. 대표적인 AI 기업의 증시 데뷔가 AI 산업의 성장성과 미국 증시를 이끌어온 AI 투자 열기를 가늠할 중요한 시험대가 될 수 있다는 점에서 관심이 집중되고 있습니다.

■ “GPU 시장 감가상각 안 통한다”...출시 6년 차 A100도 임대료 역주행

올해 주요 GPU 5종의 임대료가 모두 연초보다 올랐으며 출시 6년 차인 엔비디아 A100도 상승세를 보였습니다. AI 에이전트 사용 증가로 토큰 처리 수요가 급증하면서 구형 GPU까지 가격이 오르는 현상이 나타나, 기존 감가상각 기준의 적절성에도 의문이 제기됐습니다.

items.title: Microsoft just shared Azure’s actual revenue in dollars: $33.2 billion
items.summary: Microsoft has never disclosed Azure's quarterly revenue in dollars. But for the first time, we can see just how close it is getting to besting the biggest competitor in the market, AWS.
items.content:
Microsoft has never disclosed Azure’s quarterly revenue in dollars. It has typically only shared a growth percentage or described revenue dollar milestones in vague ways. But on Wednesday, when it posted another record-breaking quarter , it reported that Azure brought in a healthy $33.2 billion in revenue for the July–September quarter, up 48% from a year earlier.

The disclosure lets investors line up Azure’s performance more directly against Amazon Web Services and Google Cloud, whose parent companies already report cloud revenue in dollars every quarter.

Alphabet, which also reported earnings on Wednesday, said Google Cloud brought in $30.7 billion in the same quarter, putting Azure slightly ahead. But Google Cloud, which also includes Google’s Workspace subscriptions, roughly doubled its revenue from a year earlier, growing about twice as fast as Azure, according to TechCrunch’s calculations.

Azure, where businesses rent computing power to run applications, SaaS, and to build and run AI models, is now Microsoft’s largest and fastest-growing product line by the company’s own figures. It accounted for roughly 36% of Microsoft’s $92.3 billion in quarterly revenue.

Azure’s revenue was also about $850 million more than the $32.3 billion analysts expected . Azure’s 48% growth rate also topped the 44% to 45% that Microsoft CFO Amy Hood forecast on the company’s July earnings call .

Azure sits inside Agents and Infra, one of two new business segments Microsoft introduced this quarter. Microsoft previously reported three segments, Productivity and Business Processes, Intelligent Cloud and More Personal Computing. The new Agents and Infra segment, which groups Azure with Microsoft 365’s cloud business, brought in $76.8 billion , up 25% from a year earlier.

Amazon reports its earnings on Thursday. Analysts also expect its cloud, Amazon Web Services, to grow. It’s been the largest cloud since the beginning of time and no one expects Microsoft to best it right now. But with all of them reporting actual dollars, the race is on.

items.title: Google expands AI Search ads globally as core ad growth slows
items.summary: The announcement came alongside parent company Alphabet's third-quarter earnings report, which saw revenue grow 25% year over year to $127.6 billion.
items.content:
Google is bringing ads in its AI-powered Search experiences to international markets, betting that generative AI can open up new revenue opportunities even as growth in its core search advertising business slows.

The announcement came Wednesday during Alphabet’s third-quarter earnings call, as the company reported $127.6 billion in revenue, up 25% year over year. But Search advertising growth continued to decelerate, and Alphabet shares fell 8% following the results.

Google Search revenue grew 12% year over year in the third quarter, down from 17% growth in the second quarter and 19% in the first quarter. The slowdown puts added pressure on Google to turn its expanding AI features into a meaningful source of advertising revenue.

“We are now scaling high-quality ads within AI overviews in AI mode to more users and queries,” Philipp Schindler, Google’s chief business officer, said during the call with investors. “This includes taking our monetization footprint global for the first time. Today, we’re announcing the expansion of ads in AI mode into international markets alongside multi-turn ads and AI mode in the U.S.”

Google says early results suggest the formats are working. Click-through rates for sponsored product listings in AI Mode are already comparable to those for organic listings, according to Schindler. The company’s user research also indicates that people find the ads relevant.

The move builds on Google’s May announcement of new Gemini-powered ad formats, including conversational discovery ads that respond to users’ questions and sponsored recommendations integrated into AI-generated answers.

Google CEO Sundar Pichai also said that Search queries grew at their fastest year-over-year rate in five years, though he did not disclose the exact growth rate. He credited AI features with changing how people use Search, including prompting longer and more complex queries.

Queries in AI Mode are three times longer on average than traditional searches, Pichai said, while one in five AI Mode searches globally involves voice, images, or documents. Google has also surpassed 50 billion visual searches per month.

“[Search] is bringing the benefits of AI to more people than any other product in the world,” Pichai told investors. “People are using our AI features more, searching in entirely new ways. Their queries are longer, personalized, and multimodal.”

Alphabet’s Google Services division, which includes Search, generated $96.3 billion in revenue, up 11% year over year. Google Cloud revenue surged 103% to $30.7 billion.

The results follow a busy quarter for Google, including the release of Gemini 4 Argon , the growth of the Gemini app to 1 billion monthly users , and the launch of its Pixel 11 lineup .

items.title: Microsoft recorded $10 billion in revenue from OpenAI
items.summary: Microsoft said it made $10 billion in revenue from commercial arrangements with OpenAI, including revenue-sharing payments, in the quarter ending September 30. It underscores the still-enormous financial dependency of the partnership.
items.content:
Microsoft generated $10 billion in revenue from commercial arrangements with OpenAI, including revenue-sharing payments, in the quarter ended September 30, the company said in a regulatory filing on Wednesday. That represents nearly 11% of Microsoft’s total quarterly revenue of $92.3 billion, highlighting the enormous financial ties that remain between the two companies even as they increasingly compete for the same customers .

(Microsoft’s financial year begins in July, making the quarter ended September 30, 2026 the first quarter of its fiscal 2027.)

For the full 2026 fiscal year, revenue from OpenAI hit $24.1 billion. At its latest quarterly pace, Microsoft would pull in $40 billion annually from OpenAI-related arrangements.

Microsoft also reported $7.2 billion in outstanding receivables from OpenAI at the end of September, up from $6 billion at the end of June. That money represents amounts OpenAI owes for previous transactions, not additional revenue.

It’s not clear how much of Microsoft’s revenue from OpenAI came from revenue-sharing payments or Azure cloud computing services. TechCrunch has reached out for more information. In November 2025, TechCrunch reported , citing leaked documents, that Microsoft had received $865.8 million in net revenue-sharing payments from OpenAI during the first nine months of that year.

OpenAI reportedly shares 20% of its revenue with Microsoft as part of a previous deal in which the software giant invested more than $13 billion in the AI startup. (Neither the AI lab nor Microsoft have publicly confirmed this percentage.) As part of an April 2026 agreement, OpenAI is on the hook to continue sharing revenue with Microsoft through 2030, subject to a cap, even as OpenAI is allowed to work with competing cloud providers.

The companies began loosening the ties of their once-exclusive partnership in October 2025, when Microsoft relinquished its hold on OpenAI to give the startup more freedom to partner with other cloud providers. In exchange, OpenAI committed to buying an additional $250 billion in Azure services as part of an October 2025 agreement.

Microsoft’s ownership stake in OpenAI has also declined slightly from about 25% in June to 24% in September. That continues a gradual decline from roughly 27% following the October 2025 recapitalization. Microsoft did not specify what caused the dilution.

items.content:
The MPC Sample Key will be an open-source 37-key take on its budget-friendly MPC Sample.

The MPC Sample Key isn’t even formally announced yet, but Akai is already showing off what the modding community is cooking up through vibe coding. Akai has decided to embrace the explosion of hackers and custom firmware developers by giving them early access to the device, which will have open-source firmware.

It will likely run some version of the same software found on the MPC Sample , but with tweaks to accommodate the traditional keyboard, pitch, and mod wheels. Unlike the higher-end MPC Key 37, however, the Sample Key doesn’t have pads. Instead, you play back samples with the keys.

In the short Instagram Reels posted last night and today, Akai shows a number of vibe-coded mods that add synths, including Native Instruments Massive, to the device, as well as virtual analog and FM synths. One is even shown running a completely custom OS, with “several different synths in it.”

According to the clips , the same “community” features will come to the regular MPC Sample, which is also shown running a few vibe-coded synths built by Claude. That could mean Akai plans to open-source the entire MPC Sample platform.

CEO Jack O’Donnell told The Verge that inMusic brands, especially Akai, would be looking to embrace the modding community by seeding early devices to developers. These efforts will also include open-sourcing some software and providing an SDK.

items.title: Microsoft hits 10 quarters of record-breaking revenue in a row
items.summary: Whatever the future of AI might be, the current situation is still very good for Microsoft. The tech giant reported yet another record for quarterly revenue on Wednesday: $92.3 billion, a 19% increase over the year-ago quarter.
items.content:
Whatever the future of AI might be, the current situation is still very good for Microsoft. The tech giant reported yet another quarterly revenue record on Wednesday: $92.3 billion , a 19% increase over the year-ago quarter.

Microsoft has now reported record-breaking revenue for 10 quarters in a row .

This is profitable revenue, too. Microsoft reported that net income reached $36.6 billion, an increase of 32% on a GAAP basis, over the year-ago quarter.

The record-breaking income was largely driven on the strength of Microsoft Cloud, which reached $63.9 billion in revenue this quarter, an increase of 30% over the year-ago quarter, Microsoft said.

Microsoft has reorganized its business reporting into two basic segments: 1) Agents and Infra and 2) Devices and Consumer. On the flip side, revenue in Devices and Consumer was $15.5 billion, decreased of 3%, with Windows OEM and devices revenue falling 22% from the year-ago quarter.

True, not all of Microsoft’s healthy cloud revenue can be attributed to AI. Microsoft 365 accounted for nearly $28 billion. But Azure brought in the most, at $33.2 billion. And again, not all of that is necessarily AI-related. Enterprises run all sorts of the traditional software and SaaS applications on Azure.

Still, a good chunk of the revenue was from AI, because Microsoft also reported $10 billion in revenue from OpenAI . Despite branching out to AWS, Oracle, and others, OpenAI still runs a lot of its services on Microsoft’s cloud. (Anthropic runs on Azure as well.) Microsoft also said its “commercial remaining performance obligation increased 73% to $677 billion.” That represents future revenue committed under existing contracts of the AI labs.

But, like all the big cloud providers, Microsoft is also spending big to prepare to deliver on those commitments. Capital expenditures topped $45.2 billion, another all-time quarterly record.

items.content:
애플이 창사 이래 처음으로 터치스크린을 탑재한 맥북 프로를 공개했다. 스티브 잡스 창업자가 2010년 노트북 터치스크린을 강하게 비판한 이후 16년 만에 기존 입장을 바꾼 것이다. 새로운 맥북 프로는 OLED 디스플레이와 아이폰의 '다이내믹 아일랜드'까지 도입하고, 화면을 손가락으로 조작할 수 있도록 운영체제도 개선했다.

애플은 28일(현지시간) 미국 로스앤젤레스에서 신제품 발표 행사를 열고 '프로LED XDR(PROLED XDR)' 디스플레이를 탑재한 14인치와 16인치 맥북 프로를 공개했다. 가격은 14인치 M5 프로 모델이 2899달러(약 390만원), 16인치 모델이 3399달러(약 457만원)부터 시작한다. 사전 주문은 이날 시작했으며, 정식 판매는 11월6일 예정이다.

가장 큰 변화는 터치스크린이다. 사용자는 화면을 손가락으로 쓸어 웹페이지를 넘기거나, 두 손가락으로 사진을 확대하고, 창을 끌어 이동할 수 있다. 디자이너는 화면에 직접 그림을 그리고, 음악 제작자는 가상 악기를 손가락으로 연주할 수도 있다. 기존 키보드와 트랙패드 조작 방식은 그대로 유지된다.

이를 위해 애플은 '맥OS 27'에 터치 입력 기능을 추가했다. 기존 앱에서도 화면을 누르면 마우스 클릭으로 인식하도록 했으며, 개발자들이 터치에 최적화된 앱을 만들 수 있는 기능도 제공한다. 어도비 라이트룸과 다빈치 리졸브, 블렌더 등 주요 전문가용 소프트웨어도 터치 입력을 지원할 예정이다.

이번 제품은 애플의 오랜 설계 철학을 바꿨다는 점에서 의미가 크다. 잡스는 2010년 터치스크린 노트북에 대해 "인체공학적으로 끔찍하다(ergonomically terrible)"라고 비판했다. 화면을 수직으로 세운 상태에서 장시간 손을 뻗어 조작하면 사용자가 쉽게 피로해진다는 이유였다.

팀 쿡 전 CEO도 2012년 노트북과 태블릿을 결합하는 시도를 냉장고와 토스터를 합치는 것에 비유하며 부정적인 입장을 밝혔다. 현재 CEO인 존 터너스도 2021년 인터뷰에서 아이패드는 터치에, 맥은 키보드와 트랙패드에 최적화돼 있다며 이를 바꿀 필요가 없다고 말한 바 있다.

그러나 터치스크린이 윈도우 노트북에 널리 보급되고, 스마트폰과 태블릿의 터치 조작에 익숙한 세대가 늘어나면서 애플도 방향을 바꿨다. 블룸버그에 따르면 애플은 약 4년 전부터 터치스크린 맥북 프로 개발을 추진해 왔다.

디스플레이와 디자인도 크게 달라졌다. 신제품은 두 개의 OLED 발광층을 사용하는 탠덤 OLED 기술을 적용해 최대 2000니트 밝기와 1000만대 1 명암비, 최대 120Hz 주사율을 지원한다. 아이폰에서 사용하던 다이내믹 아일랜드도 맥에 처음 도입해 음악 재생과 알림, 검색, 시리 AI 등의 기능을 화면 상단에서 조작할 수 있도록 했다.

'M5 프로'와 'M5 맥스' 칩을 탑재했으며, 최대 128GB 통합 메모리와 16TB 저장장치를 지원한다. 무게는 14인치 모델이 약 1.36kg, 16인치 모델이 약 1.81kg으로 기존 제품보다 가벼워졌다. 배터리 사용 시간은 최대 24시간이다.

다만 높은 가격은 시장 확대의 변수다. IDC에 따르면 지난해 전 세계 터치스크린 노트북 출하량은 3340만대로 전년 대비 22% 증가했지만, 전체 노트북 시장에서 차지하는 비중은 16%에 그쳤다. 평균 판매 가격도 1009달러로 신형 맥북 프로의 3분의 1 수준이다.

라이언 레이스 IDC 부사장은 CNBC에 터치스크린이 윈도우 노트북에서 오랫동안 제공됐지만 구매를 결정하는 핵심 요인은 아니었다고 설명했다. 그는 애플의 터치스크린 맥북 성공 여부에 대해 "이는 전적으로 사용자 인터페이스와 소프트웨어의 문제"라고 평가했다.

items.content:
[깃허브 유니버스 26] 데이글 COO, 2억 2500만 개발자 생태계 강조

컴퓨팅 입력 :2026/10/29 06:09 수정: 2026/10/29 06:13

[샌프란시스코(미국)=김미정 기자] "세상에 새로운 깃허브가 필요하다고 생각하지 않습니다. 시대 변화에 맞춰 진화하는 인공지능(AI) 플랫폼이 필요합니다. 우리는 그렇게 하고 있습니다."

카일 데이글 깃허브 최고운영책임자(COO)는 미국 샌프란시스코에서 열린 '깃허브 유니버스 26' 기자간담회에서 엔타이어와의 경쟁에 대해 이같이 밝혔다. 토마스 돔케 전 최고경영자(CEO)가 세운 경쟁사 존재감을 인정하면서도 기존 깃허브를 발전시키는 데 집중하겠다는 입장이다.

엔타이어는 깃허브 유니버스 개막 하루 전인 27일 코드 저장과 관리부터 검토와 테스트까지 지원하는 독립형 AI 개발 플랫폼을 공개했다. 깃허브에서 하던 주요 작업을 엔타이어에서도 처리할 수 있도록 한 것이다.

엔타이어가 깃허브와 차별화하려는 핵심 영역은 코드 검토다. AI가 코드를 빠르게 작성해도 사람이 변경 내용을 일일이 확인해야 한다면 전체 개발 속도를 높이는 데 한계가 있다는 판단이다. 이를 해결하기 위해 깃허브 핵심 협업 기능인 '풀 리퀘스트'를 대체하는 '트레일스'를 플랫폼에 도입했다.

풀 리퀘스트는 변경된 코드를 기존 프로젝트에 합치기 전 검토를 요청하는 기능이다. 트레일스는 여러 AI 에이전트가 코드 품질을 평가하고 발견한 문제를 반복적으로 수정하도록 설계됐다. 엔타이어는 모든 평가 기준을 충족하면 개발자가 변경된 코드를 전부 읽지 않고도 기존 프로젝트에 합칠 수 있다고 설명했다.

두 회사 경쟁 구도에는 깃허브 모회사 마이크로소프트 투자 관계도 얽혀 있다. 엔타이어가 지난 2월 10일 발표한 6000만 달러 규모 시드 투자에는 마이크로소프트의 벤처투자 조직 M12가 참여했다. 이는 펠리시스가 주도하고 마드로나 등이 함께한 투자였다. 당시 엔타이어 기업가치는 3억 달러로 평가됐으며 M12의 개별 투자액은 공개되지 않았다.

M12는 투자 당시부터 AI 에이전트와 개발자의 협업 방식에 주목한 것으로 전해졌다. 미셸 곤잘레스 M12 총괄은 엔타이어가 사람과 에이전트 협업을 위한 플랫폼을 처음부터 새로 설계하고 있다고 평가하며 투자 배경을 설명한 바 있다. 기존 개발 도구에 AI 기능을 추가하는 것을 넘어 개발 환경 자체를 바꾸려는 시도에 투자한 셈이다.

간담회에서도 데이글 COO는 M12가 깃허브뿐 아니라 마이크로소프트 제품과 경쟁하는 개발사에도 자주 투자한다고 답했다. 개발자가 가장 좋은 도구를 사용할 수 있어야 한다는 점을 재차 강조했다.

이날 깃허브는 플랫폼 규모 성장과 인프라 추가 구축 계획을 의지를 밝혔다. 데이글 COO는 전 세계 2억2500만 명 이상 개발자를 지원하는 환경에서 AI 에이전트를 활용하는 작업 방식에 맞춰 개발의 핵심 기능을 개선하고 있다고 설명했다.

그는 깃허브 개발자 커뮤니티도 경쟁력으로 제시했다. 소프트웨어(SW) 개발 방식이 빠르게 바뀔수록 개발자가 결과물을 공유하고 함께 배우는 커뮤니티가 중요해진다는 판단에서다. 엔타이어가 새로운 코드 검토 방식으로 기존 개발 환경을 바꾸려 한다면 깃허브는 축적한 인프라와 커뮤니티를 바탕으로 변화에 대응하겠다는 구도다.

데이글 COO는 "개발자들이 가장 좋은 도구를 사용할 수 있기를 바란다"며 "필요한 것은 시대 변화에 맞춰 진화하는 플랫폼"이라고 강조했다.

items.content:
In association with Atlan

Across a business, any number of AI platforms, systems, and tools may be at work simultaneously—for example, AI-powered customer platforms, conversational assistants, and workflow and process automation tools. Each one is sophisticated, advanced, and quick to respond. But, when set to work, the outcomes and actions that emerge may be wrong, confused, or lacking a proper understanding of the business. Many organizations find themselves in this situation—and it could be one of key reasons they struggle to extract returns on their AI investments.

An MIT Technology Review Insights poll finds that while every organization surveyed is using AI today to some degree, fewer than one in five (16%) are extracting transformative value from their deployments. The largest percentage of respondents (40%) say they are seeing moderate gains in specific tasks or teams, while 21% report meaningful gains, leaving 23% that are seeing minimal returns or none at all.

Companies are mostly still piloting AI use cases (according to 38% of respondents) or using it to assist employees’ work with tools like co-pilots or chat assistants (35%). Just 12% of enterprises have AI agents in production and 3% say they are using AI to do most of the work in key processes.

“There’s a big gap between what the models are capable of and how the models are actually being useful inside organizations,” says Prukalpa Sankar, co-founder of Atlan. “For every real-life intent and purpose, artificial general intelligence is already here. It’s just not really useful in most companies today.”

The missing layer, Sankar says, is context, or how well AI understands a business. A context layer is the architectural infrastructure that sits between an organization’s business systems (for example, systems of record and data, and its AI platforms). It translates enterprise intelligence into governed, machine-usable context for AI agents or models and helps knowledge compound. “Without a context layer for AI, it’s almost like you’re hiring the smartest intern in the world, blindfolding them, and throwing them into your organization,” Sankar says.

Google’s year-over-year search query growth rate is ‘the highest it’s been in the last five years.’

Google parent company Alphabet says that its AI investments are leading to a big growth in searches year-over-year, as noted in its Q3 2026 earnings today .

“Our AI investments are driving overall Search query growth, including commercial queries,” CEO Sundar Pichai says in a statement. “In fact, our year-over-year query growth rate is the highest it’s been in the last five years.”

The earnings follow a packed quarter for Google, including the announcement of its Gemini 4 Argon frontier model (which it released widely this month ); crossing 1 billion monthly users in Gemini ; the reveal of the first five Googlebook laptops ; a price hike for the Google TV Streamer ; renaming NotebookLM to Gemini Notebook ; the launch of the Pixel 11 line of smartphones, the new Pixel Watch , and the forthcoming Pixel Tag ; and a major shakeup of its top AI leadership that included former DeepMind leader Demis Hassabis stepping into a chair role .

items.content:
구글이 1년 만에 AI 모델 종합 성능 평가에서 세계 1위를 탈환했다. 새로 공개한 '제미나이 4 카본(Gemini 4 Carbon)'은 아티피셜 애널리시스(AA) 평가에서 앤트로픽의 '클로드 오퍼스 5.5'와 오픈AI의 'GPT-6 아스트라'를 제치고 정상에 올랐다. 특히 사이버 보안과 장시간 자율 작업 능력을 대폭 개선했으며, 복잡한 소프트웨어의 취약점을 찾아내고 공격 가능성을 검증한 뒤 수정하는 작업에서 최고 수준의 성능을 기록했다.

구글 딥마인드는 28일(현지시간) 공식 블로그 를 통해 플래그십 모델인 제미나이 4 카본을 발표했다. 지난 9월 말 '제미나이 4 아르곤'을 처음 공개하고 10월13일 개발자들에게 정식 출시한 지 약 2주 만이다.

코라이 카부쿠오글루 구글 딥마인드 수석 부사장은 "제미나이 4 카본은 최고 수준의 사이버 보안과 장시간 작업 수행 능력을 갖춘 우리의 가장 강력한 모델"이라고 소개했다. 그는 연구진과 AI 모델이 함께 기술 개발 속도를 높이는 동시에 안전장치도 강화하고 있다고 설명했다.

가장 눈에 띄는 것은 외부 성능 평가 결과다. 아티피셜 애널리시스 인텔리전스 인덱스(AAII)에서 카본은 추론 강도 '하이(high)' 기준 59점을 기록해 평가 대상 52개 모델 중 1위를 차지했다. 클로드 오퍼스 5.5(58점)와 GPT-6 아스트라(57점)를 앞섰으며, 직전 모델인 아르곤(50점)과는 9점 차이를 보였다. 이 지표는 코딩과 추론, 과학 문제 해결, 전문 업무 등을 평가한 9개 벤치마크를 종합한 것이다.

구글이 이 평가에서 정상을 차지한 것은 약 11개월 만이다. 지난해 11월18일 출시한 '제미나이 3 프로'는 당시 AAII에서 'GPT-5.1'을 3점 차이로 제치고 1위를 기록했다. 이후 오픈AI와 앤트로픽 등이 신모델을 출시하며 선두가 바뀌었고, 구글은 이번 카본으로 다시 1위를 차지했다.

순다르 피차이 구글 CEO는 X를 통해 "불과 2주 전 출시한 아르곤에 이어 카본은 우리가 얼마나 빠르게 기술 혁신을 추진하고 있는지 보여주는 좋은 사례"라고 밝혔다. 구글이 신모델 출시 주기를 단축하며 오픈AI와 앤트로픽에 대한 공세를 강화하고 있다는 의미다.

Google’s Gemini 4 Carbon is the new #1 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v5, and second only to Claude Opus 5.5 on the Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index

Gemini 4 Carbon scores 59 on Intelligence Index v5, driven by leading performance in complex reasoning,… pic.twitter.com/gSH65FSKzL

구글이 특히 강조한 특징은 장시간에 걸쳐 복잡한 작업을 자율적으로 수행하는 능력이다. 단순히 주어진 명령에 따라 코드를 작성하는 데 그치지 않고, 여러 단계의 작업을 계획하고 실패한 접근법을 수정하면서 문제 해결을 이어가도록 설계됐다.

구글에 따르면 내부 연구진은 카본이 며칠 동안 하나의 엔지니어링 작업을 수행하며 대규모 코드에서 복잡한 오류의 원인을 추적하고 수정하는 사례를 확인했다. 작업 범위를 벗어나는 행동은 26%, 필요한 작업을 수행하지 못하는 사례는 29% 감소했다.

코딩 평가에서도 성능 향상이 확인됐다. AA의 '코딩 에이전트 지수'에서 카본은 59점을 기록해 클로드 오퍼스 5.5(62점)에 이어 2위를 차지했다. '터미널벤치 4.0'에서는 64%, 복잡한 소프트웨어 개발 능력을 측정하는 '프론티어코드 v1.1'에서는 51%로 모두 2위에 올랐다. 구글이 상대적으로 약세를 보였던 코딩 에이전트 분야에서 선두권에 진입했다는 평가다.

사이버 보안에서는 더 뚜렷한 성과를 보였다. 실제 소프트웨어에서 보안 취약점을 찾아내는 'SEC-벤치 프로'에서 88.2%, 발견한 취약점이 실제 공격에 이용될 수 있는지 검증하는 '익스플로잇짐(ExploitGym)'에서 54.8%, 취약점을 수정하는 'CWE-벤치'에서 71.0%를 기록했다. 구글은 세 평가 모두 최고 수준의 성적이라고 밝혔다.

이는 AI가 취약점을 발견하는 데 그치지 않고 실제 위험성을 확인하고 수정 코드를 작성하는 과정까지 수행할 수 있다는 의미다. 구글은 자체 시험에서 카본의 안전한 코드 생성 성공률이 아르곤의 두 배 이상으로 높아졌다고 밝혔다. 크롬 개발팀에서는 다른 AI 연구소의 대형 모델과 비교해 고품질 보안 패치를 생성하는 성능이 10배 이상 높았다는 결과도 나왔다.

모델 자체의 안전성도 개선했다. 구글 내부 평가에서 심각한 정렬 위반 경고는 약 80%, 충분한 근거 없이 사실을 주장하는 행동은 약 50% 감소했다. 외부 지시문으로 AI의 행동을 조작하는 프롬프트 인젝션 공격 평가에서도 공격 성공률이 아르곤의 0.7%에서 0%로 낮아졌다.

또 다른 AI 평가업체 발스 AI의 전문 업무 평가에서도 최상위권에 올랐다. 29개 모델을 대상으로 금융·법률·코딩·세무 업무를 종합 평가한 '발스 인덱스 v2.2'에서 카본은 70.36%로 2위를 기록했다.

1위인 클로드 소네트 5.5(70.85%)에 근소하게 뒤졌지만, 클로드 오퍼스 5.5(70.18%)는 앞섰다. 특히 금융 종합 지수와 법률 연구 벤치마크에서는 모두 1위를 차지했으며, 금융 모델링 2위, 세무 에이전트 3위에 올랐다. AA가 추론과 지식, 코딩 등 전반적인 AI 능력을 평가한다면, 발스 AI는 금융·법률·세무 등 실제 전문 업무 수행 능력에 초점을 맞춘다.

다만 전문 업무 능력 향상에는 처리 시간과 토큰 사용량 증가가 뒤따랐다. 발스 AI에 따르면 카본은 아르곤보다 출력 토큰을 64% 더 사용했으며, 금융·세무 에이전트 작업에는 두 배 이상 시간이 걸렸다. 법률 연구는 작업당 50분 넘게 소요됐다. 발스 AI는 카본이 더 철저하게 작업을 수행하는 대신 속도를 희생했다고 분석했다.

반대로 금융 모델링과 터미널 코딩에서는 아르곤보다 빠르고 정확했으며, 종합 평가의 작업당 비용도 10.51달러로 '클로드 소네트 5.5(18.70달러)'보다 낮았다.

Google DeepMind’s Gemini 4 Carbon debuts at #2 on the Vals Index v2.2.

It also takes #1 on both the Finance Index and our Legal Research Benchmark. pic.twitter.com/GCVsst7Hk6

AA의 전문 업무 평가에서는 경쟁 모델에 뒤졌다. 문서 작성과 분석 등의 능력을 측정하는 'AA-브리프케이스'에서 카본은 1609점을 기록해 아르곤(1483점)보다 126점 상승했지만, '키미 K3.1 프로(1678점)' '뮤즈 원더(1659점)' '그록 4.7(1638점)'에는 미치지 못했다.

사실관계에 대한 지식과 정확성을 평가하는 'AA-옴니사이언스'에서는 54점으로 전체 1위를 차지했다. 클로드 오퍼스 5.5(48점)를 6점 앞섰으며, 정답률도 아르곤의 48%에서 58%로 상승했다. 그러나 이 평가에서 측정한 환각률은 4%에서 11%로 높아졌다. 다만 같은 평가에서 클로드 오퍼스 5.5와 GPT-6 아스트라는 각각 50%를 기록했다. AA는 카본의 환각률이 아르곤에 이어 두 번째로 낮다고 평가했다.

카본은 최대 100만토큰의 컨텍스트를 지원하며 텍스트와 이미지, 음성, 영상을 입력받을 수 있다. 출력은 텍스트로 제공된다. 모델의 매개변수 규모나 구체적인 학습 구조는 공개되지 않았다.

가격은 아르곤과 같은 수준으로 책정했다. 초기 API 가격은 입력 토큰 100만개당 2달러, 출력 100만개당 10달러다. 할인 기간이 끝나면 각각 4달러와 20달러로 두 배 오른다. 할인 종료 시점은 공개하지 않았다.

AA가 할인 종료 후 정가를 기준으로 평가한 작업당 비용은 7.76달러로, 클로드 오퍼스 5.5(10.04달러)보다 약 23% 저렴하지만 GPT-6 아스트라(6.25달러)보다는 비싸다. 카본이 전체 평가에서 생성한 출력 토큰량은 약 2억개로 비교 모델의 중앙값인 6400만개의 3배를 넘었다. 실제 업무에서는 토큰 단가와 함께 작업을 완료하는 데 필요한 토큰량과 처리 시간도 비용을 결정하는 요소다.

카본은 당장 모든 이용자가 사용할 수 있는 것은 아니다. 구글은 이번 주부터 일부 사이버 보안 전문가에게 모델을 제공하고, '페어윈드(Fairwind)' 프로그램을 통해 검증된 협력사로 접근권을 확대할 예정이다. 미국 정부의 출시 전 모델 평가 절차에도 참여하고 있다.

일반 개발자와 기업, 소비자를 대상으로 한 정식 출시 일정은 아직 공개되지 않았다. 구글은 초기 이용자들의 피드백을 바탕으로 안전장치를 검증한 뒤 이용 대상을 넓힐 계획이다.

items.title: Microsoft reveals strong cloud growth amid financial reporting overhaul
items.summary: Microsoft just posted the first quarter of its 2027 fiscal financial results. The software maker made $92.3 billion in revenue and a net income of $33.6 billion during Q1. Revenue is up 19 percent, and net income has increased by 32 percent. It's a new financial year for Microsof
items.content:
Windows and Xbox revenues have declined during Microsoft’s first quarter of the 2027 financial year.

Microsoft just posted the first quarter of its 2027 fiscal financial results. The software maker made $92.3 billion in revenue and a net income of $33.6 billion during Q1. Revenue is up 19 percent, and net income has increased by 32 percent.

It’s a new financial year for Microsoft, so the company is changing up how it reports its finances by splitting its businesses into two segments for the first time. Gone are the previous segments: Productivity and Business Processes, Intelligent Cloud, and More Personal Computing. It’s now just Agents and Infra, and Devices and Consumer.

Agents and Infra, which includes businesses like Azure, Microsoft 365 commercial and consumer, and server products, makes up 83 percent ($76.8 billion) of the overall $92.3 billion of Microsoft’s revenue and has increased 25 percent year-over-year. The big changes to Microsoft’s financial reporting also mean we will now see the company disclose Azure revenue on a quarterly basis. Azure contributed $33.17 billion in revenue this quarter, up 48 percent year-over-year.

Devices and Consumer, which includes Windows, Xbox, Surface, and Microsoft’s search and advertising businesses, makes up the remaining 17 percent ($15.5 billion) of Microsoft’s $92.3 billion in revenues this quarter — a decrease of three percent.

Windows OEM and devices revenue is down 22 percent year-over-year, amid a RAMageddon crisis that has seen the overall PC market dropped by 20 percent in the recent quarter. Microsoft blames the revenue drop on the benefit of Windows 10 end of support during the prior year, as well as OEM inventory drawdowns and a weaker PC market.

Microsoft launched Intel- and Qualcomm-powered Surface Pro 12 and Surface Laptop 8 devices just before its new financial year began, and the company even refreshed its smaller Surface Pro and Surface Laptop with Qualcomm’s X2 Plus chips during the quarter. Surface prices are higher than ever thanks to RAMageddon , and the PC market looks like it’s going to go through a very tough time during Microsoft’s 2027 financial year and beyond.

Microsoft CFO Amy Hood said on the company’s earnings call that she expects Windows OEM revenue to decline again next quarter, around “the mid 30s,” and a decline is expected to continue throughout the 2027 financial year. Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella also remarked on the company’s new hybrid AI push for Windows during the earnings call. “We are executing on our vision to bring hybrid intelligence to every desk in every home, making every PC a secure agent box,” said Nadella. “As more capable models run locally, we see an opportunity to make more intelligence effectively unmetered.”

Microsoft and Nvidia unveiled a range of RTX Spark laptops earlier this month, including the Surface Laptop Ultra. The laptops ship with up to 128GB of unified memory, and are capable of running recent frontier models locally.

The first quarter of the 2027 financial year for Xbox has been dominated by a “reset” with thousands of layoffs and studios spun off. The layoffs aren’t over yet, with rumors more could arrive in November and January. In a memo earlier this year, Xbox CEO Asha Sharma said “we will return Xbox to player and revenue growth” by the end of fiscal year 2027 (which runs through next June).

The aim, as Sharma puts it, is to “scale what works” so that by fiscal year 2030 Xbox is “halfway to our long-term daily-player goal with sustained double-digit growth in players and engagement and industry leading margins.” Sharma posted on X that Xbox was “making progress, with a lot more work ahead.” Sharma also revealed that PC platform revenue has grown in double digits this quarter, and that “console sales remain constrained by supply, with more demand than consoles available.”

Hood says Xbox hardware revenue will decline again next quarter, but Xbox content and services revenue is expected to increase in the “mid to high single digits.” Sharma says Microsoft is “working to get more consoles into players’ hands, including through our expanded refurbishment program.”

Microsoft’s cloud revenues were really the star of the earnings show again this quarter, a phrase I seem to always write every few months. Microsoft Cloud revenue contributed $63.9 billion towards Microsoft’s revenues this quarter, almost 70 percent. That’s up 30 percent year-over-year, thanks to strong demand for Azure and Microsoft 365 commercial cloud.

Nadella also discussed his vision for Microsoft’s own AI models on the company’s earnings call. “We also continue to make rapid progress with our first-party models,” said Nadella. “Our goal is to advance the cost to outcome frontier, which means delivering capabilities comparable to leading models within three to six months of their release at a fraction of the training cost, thereby allowing us to transfer those cost benefits to customers.”

items.content:
3.75~4.00%로 결정…2명 인상 주장

금융 입력 :2026/10/29 05:18 수정: 2026/10/29 07:47

미국 연방준비제도(연준)가 27~28일(현지시간) 연 공개시장위원회(FOMC)에서 연방기금금리 범위를 현행과 같은 수준인 3.75%~4.00%로 동결하기로 결정했다.

인플레이션 우려 속에서도 지난 9월 금리를 0.25%p 상향 조정한 이후, 금융 및 신용 여건이 긴축됐다는 점에서 금리를 유지하기로 했다.

이번 결정은 FOMC 위원 12명 중 2명이 금리 동결에 반대했다. FOMC 위원 12명 중 2명인 리사 쿡 연준이사와 베스 해맥 클리블랜드 연방은행 총재는 0.25%p 금리 인상을 주장했다. 리사 쿡 이사는 조 바이든 대통령 임명으로 2022년 연준에 합류한 이후 처음으로 반대표를 던졌다.

FOMC 회의 직후 낸 연준 성명서에 따르면 인플레이션이 여전히 높은 수준이지만, 추가 인상 전 더 많은 데이터가 축적되기를 기다리고 있다. 이어 " 더 많은 정보가 축적되는 것은 위원회가 인플레이션을 위원회의 목표치인 2%로 적시에 되돌리기에 적절한 정책 기조를 결정하는 데 도움이 될 것"이라며 " 물가 안정을 달성할 것"이라고 부연했다.

케빈 워시 연준 의장은 "경제가 여전히 강력하다"며 "고용 역시 매우 긍정적으로 42주 이동 평균 실업보험 청구 건은 수 십년 만에 최저 수준"이라고 평가했다. 올해 상반기 미국 경제성장률 수정치는 기존 1.8%에서 2.4%로 상향 조정됐다. 4주 이동 평균 신규 실업보험 청구 건수는 약 19만7000건대로 20만건을 밑돌았다.

그는 물가 압력이 여전하지만 지난 9월 FOMC에서 0.25%p 금리를 인상한 이후 금융 및 신용 여건이 긴축되기 시작했다는 점을 언급했다. 워시 의장은 " 기업과 가계 일부에서 대출 및 신용 조건이 타이트해졌으며, 시장 참여자들이 자본 배분에 있어 더욱 까다로워지고(discerning) 있다"며 " 전반적인 금융 여건이 지나치게 긴축된 상태라고 보기는 어렵다"고 설명했다.

또 그는 "높은 금리가 인공지능(AI) 인프라 구축 등 전반적인 투자 환경에도 영향을 미쳐, 투자자들이 투자 대상을 보다 엄격하게 선별하고 있다"고 말했다.

이번 금리 결정을 두고 11월 3일 진행되는 중간선거를 의식한 것이라는 분석도 제기된다. 선거를 코앞에 두고 금리를 올리고 싶어 하지 않을 것이라고 추측인 셈이다. 그동안 도널드 트럼프 미국 대통령은 지금보다 금리가 훨씬 낮아야 한다고 비판해왔다. 케빈 워시 의장은 " 회의 기간 중 정치적 상황이나 선거에 대한 언급은 전혀 없었으며 정치적 고려는 결코 작용하지 않았다"고 선을 그었다.

오는 12월 FOMC를 두고 금리 인상이 단행될지 귀추가 주목된다. 선물 시장에서는 추가 금리 인상을 점치고 있다. 2027년에도 한 두 차례 금리 인상을 반영하고 있다.

워시 의장은 향후 금리 경로를 미리 알려주는 포워드 가이던스를 선호하지 않는다는 기존 소신을 강조했다. 그는 "예외적으로 2008년 금융위기 같은 극단적인 위기 상황이 아니라면, 현재처럼 경제가 강력한 시기에는 이를 활용하지 않겠다"고 말했다.

이밖에 2027년 FOMC 회의 방식을 변경해 연간 금리 결정 회의 횟수를 줄일 수 있음을 시사했다. 2027년 여덟 번의 회의 중 한 번은 연방기금금리 결정을 하지 않고, 2028년에는 두 차례 금리 결정보다는 광범위한 통화정책 전략에 집중한다는 계획이다. 케빈 워시 의장은 " 연간 8회 회의가 FOMC에 적절한 숫자라고 믿지만, 2027년에는 한 차례 회의가 광범위한 통화정책 전략에만 독점적으로 집중할 것"이라며 " 연방기금금리에 대한 투표나 정책 성명서를 단행하지 않는다"고 말했다. 이어 그는 "나머지는 정규 FOMC 정책 결정 회의가 될 것이며, 2028년에는 전략 논의에 전념하는 회의 2회와 정책 결정을 위한 회의 6회를 갖게 될 것으로 기대한다"고 설명했다.

앤드루 데이비스 브린 마르 트러스트 투자 전략 총괄이자 전 노동통계국(BLS) 분석가는 CNBC에 "연준이 관망하고 있다"며 " 현재 사이클 상 위치를 고려할 때 이는 타당하다고 생각한다"고 진단했다. 데이비스 분석가는 "경제는 둔화하고 있지만, 둔화와 붕괴는 서로 다른 것"이라며 " 금리를 동결함으로써 정책입안자들은 9월의 금리 인상과 최근의 장기 차입 비용 상승에 경제가 어떻게 반응하고 있는지 평가할 수 있는 더 많은 시간을 갖게 된다"고 전했다.

한편, 주요 증시는 상승 마감했다. 다우존스 산업평균지수는 전 거래일 대비 0.24%, S&P 500 지수는 0.33%, 나스닥 종합지수는 0.32% 상승했다.

The maximum configuration is $4,400 more expensive than a fully specced version of the last MacBook Pro.

With an OLED display and touchscreen capabilities , it’s no surprise that the new MacBook Pro Apple announced today is more expensive than the MBP announced earlier this year . But upgrading the base models that start at $2,899 for the 14-inch, and $3,399 for the 16-inch, with every premium hardware option that Apple offers pushes those prices to an eye-watering $14,249 and $14,549, respectively.

Both of those premium configurations include the M5 Max chip with an 18-core CPU and 40-core GPU, $150 worth of nano-texture glass, 128GB of memory that adds an extra $2,000, and 16TB of storage which is the real budget breaker here thanks to the ongoing memory shortage .

Maximizing the configuration of the previous 16-inch version of the MacBook Pro topped out at $10,149, according to MacRumors , but today’s $14,549 price is a result of the 16TB storage option that Apple now offers which adds an extra $7,000 to the new MacBook Pro’s price. If you only upgrade the new 16-inch model to 8TB of storage, a $3,000 option, the fully specced price is $10,549, or $400 more expensive than its predecessor.

2026년 첫 9개월 연결 매출 576억 디르함으로 전년 동기 대비 10.0% 증가 2026년 첫 9개월 연결 순이익 172억 디르함으로 전년 동기 대비 45.9% 증가 그룹 전체 가입자 수 2억 5480만 명 달성 창립 50주년 맞아 에티살랏이라는 이름으로 새로운 성장 시대 개막 아부다비, 아랍에미리트 , 2026년 10월 28일 /PRNewswire/ -- 에티살랏(etisalat)이 오늘 2026년 3분기 연결 재무 실적을 발표하며, 전년 동기 대비 6.9% 증가한 195억 디르함(AED)의 연결 매출을 기록했다고 보고했다. 2026년 1~9월 연결 매출은 전년 동기 대비 10.0% 증가한 576억 디르함을 달성했다. 3분기 연결 순이익은 112억 디르함을 기록했으며, 2026년 1~9월 연결 순이익은 전년 동기 대비 45.9% 증가한 172억 디르함에 달했다. 연결성, 주권형 디지털 인프라, 인공지능(AI) 분야에서 고부가가치 역량을 지속적으로 강화하고 체계적인 포트폴리오 관리를 이어간 결과다.

etisalat GCEO Masood M.Sharif

3분기 EBITDA는 전년 동기 대비 5.1% 증가한 90억 디르함을 기록했으며, EBITDA 이익률은 46.1%였다. 2026년 1~9월 EBITDA는 전년 동기 대비 10.3% 증가한 267억 디르함, EBITDA 이익률은 46.4%를 기록했다.

에티살랏의 2026년 3분기 전체 가입자 수는 전년 동기 대비 29.4% 증가한 2억 5480만 명에 달했다. 아랍에미리트(UAE) 내 가입자 수는 첨단 디지털 서비스와 지능형 연결 서비스에 대한 높은 수요에 힘입어 전년 동기 대비 5.2% 증가한 1650만 명을 기록했다.

에티살랏은 이번 분기에 보유 중이던 보다폰 그룹(Vodafone Group) 지분 전량 매각도 완료하면서 최종 배당금을 포함해 총 219억 디르함의 대금을 확보했으며, 약 80억 디르함의 이익을 거뒀다. 이번 거래는 그룹의 분기 실적에 기여하고 재무적 유연성을 한층 높였다.

창립 50주년을 맞은 에티살랏은 AI를 기반으로 운영되며 AI 활용을 뒷받침하는 선도적인 통신사가 되겠다는 새로운 비전을 제시하고, 에티살랏이라는 이름으로 도약에 나섰다. 이는 AI 시대에 연결성이 수행하는 핵심 역할을 상징한다. 이러한 포부는 디지털 서비스, 클라우드, 사이버 보안, AI, 인프라, 핀테크 전반에서 축적한 역량을 바탕으로 하며, AI를 핵심에 둔 탄탄한 통신 사업 기반을 중심으로 이러한 역량을 더욱 집중해 나간다는 구상이다.

첨단 기술과 AI의 글로벌 허브로 도약하려는 UAE의 목표를 바탕으로, 에티살랏은 2030년까지 국제 통신 용량을 현재의 25배가 넘는 초당 500테라비트(Tbps) 이상으로 확대할 계획이다. 이와 함께 연결 효율성과 안정성을 높이기 위한 다양한 통신 경로를 개발해 첨단 저지연 성능을 제공할 예정이다. 이는 신기술을 지원하고 지식 기반의 혁신 주도 경제를 실현하는 핵심 기반으로서 디지털 인프라의 중요성을 재확인한다.

에티살랏의 마수드 M. 샤리프 마흐무드(Masood M. Sharif Mahmood) 그룹 최고경영자(CEO) 는 "2026년 3분기 실적은 우리 사업 모델의 회복탄력성과 성장 기회를 실질적인 성과로 전환하는 체계적인 실행력을 보여준다. 연결 매출은 전년 동기 대비 6.9% 증가한 195억 디르함, EBITDA는 5.1% 증가한 90억 디르함을 기록했으며, EBITDA 이익률은 46.1%에 달했다. 이러한 실적은 핵심 연결성 사업의 경쟁력과 철저한 실행력을 반영한다. 우리의 집중력과 이러한 강점은 탁월한 성과를 달성하고 이해관계자를 위한 장기적 가치를 창출할 수 있다는 자신감의 토대다"라고 말했다.

마수드 CEO 는 이어 "지난 수년간 에티살랏은 AI, 클라우드 컴퓨팅, 사이버 보안, 디지털 서비스, 핀테크 전반에 걸쳐 광범위한 첨단 역량을 아우르는 통합 포트폴리오를 구축해 왔다. 오늘날 AI가 기업과 정부의 핵심 업무에 더욱 깊숙이 통합되면서 이를 구동하는 기반인 연결성, 컴퓨팅, 보안 인프라의 중요성도 커지고 있다. 그룹이 이러한 변화를 뒷받침하는 핵심 기업으로 확고히 자리매김한 만큼, 우리는 이 광범위한 전환을 이끄는 안전한 디지털 인프라와 초고속 연결 서비스를 지속적으로 제공할 것이다"라고 덧붙였다.

또한 그는 "'통신'을 뜻하는 에티살랏 브랜드는 이를 통해 새롭고 더욱 깊은 의미를 담은 사명을 갖게 됐다. 우리에게 연결성은 더 이상 단순히 데이터를 전송하는 데 그치지 않는다. 미래를 결정할 인프라와 지능형 플랫폼을 구축하고 운영함으로써 현대 디지털 경제를 뒷받침하는 것을 의미한다"고 설명했다.

마수드 CEO 는 끝으로 "에티살랏은 지속 가능한 가치를 창출하고 기술 발전을 직접적이고 실질적인 사업적 및 경제적 성과로 전환하는 역량을 입증해 왔다. 수십 년에 걸친 전략적 성과와 오랜 고객 관계, 높은 운영 효율성, 최상의 준비 태세와 안정성을 갖추도록 설계된 인프라를 바탕으로 미래 네트워크를 구현하고, 역내 디지털 경제의 기반을 강화하며, 글로벌 디지털 경제의 중심에 있는 UAE의 입지를 공고히 하는 데 계속 집중할 것이다. 에티살랏은 다음 50년의 여정을 시작하며 UAE 지도부의 미래 지향적 비전을 토대로 전진하고, 확고한 자신감으로 투자를 이어가 세계 무대에서 경쟁하고 선도하겠다는 의지를 새롭게 다진다"고 밝혔다.

items.content:
Gemini 4 Carbon is outperforming the top models from OpenAI and Anthropic on some benchmarks.

Google has released its latest frontier model, Gemini 4 Carbon, offering “significant gains” in coding, agentic tasks, and cybersecurity. In an announcement on Wednesday , Google highlights Carbon’s top spot on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index (v5.0) benchmark, with Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra trailing behind.

The new Gemini 4 Carbon model offers improvements over Argon, which Google released earlier this month. It’s currently only available to a select group of cybersecurity defense companies, but it will eventually expand to other partners in its Fairwind Program .

The company says Carbon reflects the “pace at which we’re pushing the frontier forward,” coming with a “significant leap” in cyberdefense that makes it better at finding vulnerabilities and generating secure code. Carbon currently holds the number one spot on SEC-bench Pro , a benchmark that measures an AI model’s ability to discover real-world bugs, and ExploitGym , which measures how a model can turn a vulnerability into exploits.

Google says Gemini 4 Carbon is built for completing longer tasks, adding that its internal teams have seen it “run for days to persist through dead ends to tackle complex, multi-step engineering tasks.” It’s also better at avoiding shortcuts, resisting prompt injection attacks, and collaborating with users, according to Google. Carbon is supposed to offer more “transparency and honesty” as well, by cutting “unsupported claims” by two times when compared to Argon.

It will launch at the same competitive introductory price as Argon, at $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens.

items.title: Hacker stole personnel data about thousands of Homeland Security employees, including CBP and ICE agents
items.summary: A hacker obtained personally identifiable information about more than 40,000 Homeland Security staffers, which has since been published online.
items.content:
Personally identifiable information belonging to thousands of U.S. Department of Homeland Security employees has been published online after a hacker stole reams of data in a previously undisclosed breach at the government department earlier this year.

The breach includes names, job titles, and work contact information, such as email addresses, cell phone numbers, and office locations, of more than 40,000 people who work for the federal department, including border and immigration agents, cybersecurity staffers, and senior department officials.

A hacker who goes by the handle Department of Peace claimed they obtained the data from an Okta single sign-on system used by Homeland Security to allow employees and contractors across its various agencies to log in to its central network. The Okta system also contains IT and log-in records associated with the employees’ user account, including details about which systems and internal apps they are permitted to access.

More than half of the dataset — some 21,000 records — relate to employees with U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP), who work at airports and other ports of entry.

The data also contains records associated with another 10,000 employees of Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) and its Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) unit, and just under a 1,000 employees who work at U.S. cybersecurity defense agency CISA.

Thousands of additional records relate to staff who work at the department’s headquarters and its other agencies, including U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services and the Federal Protective Service.

“They have our information, so it’s only fair that we have theirs,” said Department of Peace in a note left with the data, which TechCrunch has seen. The hacker did not respond to TechCrunch’s email requesting comment and with questions about how the breach was carried out.

This is the latest data breach to hit the U.S. government in recent months, following earlier hacks involving the theft of thousands of FBI agents’ personnel records and the personal information of millions of serving and former military service personnel from the Pentagon’s human resources unit . It’s also the second breach involving Homeland Security this year, after the same hacker claimed to have taken thousands of contracts between the department and the private sector, including defense contractors and surveillance vendors.

The latest batch of breached data, which appears authentic, offers a rare — albeit incomplete — view into the scale and operations of Homeland Security, whose deportations, arbitrary detentions, and killings of U.S. citizens under its leadership have become a key issue for voters ahead of the upcoming U.S. midterm elections.

The stolen Homeland Security data was provided to journalist and hacker maia arson crimew, who then shared a copy with DDoSecrets , a nonprofit collective that hosts leaked datasets in the public interest.

TechCrunch verified a portion of the data as authentic by matching the names of several known Homeland Security employees against an offline copy of the database. The thousands of employee directory records appear to have been exfiltrated around mid-August, according to the timestamps on each person’s record. The number of leaked records is equivalent to about one-fifth of Homeland Security’s workforce, which totals around 220,000 staff .

It’s unclear whether the vulnerability that allowed the breach has been fixed or if Homeland Security is aware of the data theft.

A spokesperson for Homeland Security did not immediately respond to TechCrunch’s request for comment about the breach.

When reached, Okta said it was aware of this report. “Okta is secure, and we have no evidence our data or systems were compromised,” a spokesperson said.

While the leaked data includes identifiable information about agents and officers, the dataset also reveals more about the surveillance technologies and cybersecurity tools that Homeland Security employees may be able to access. Critics have called for investigations into tech companies that fund or provide their technology to ICE.

The leaked data contains information about employees’ membership in user groups within the department’s Active Directory, a system that controls access to the department’s internal tools, services, and third-party offerings used for work.

Most of the Homeland Security employees in the dataset were members of the user group that had access to Microsoft 365, the tech giant’s cloud service that hosts the agency’s emails and files, as well as user groups for accessing Adobe Acrobat, Citrix, and other typical desktop software.

The data also shows that around 4,500 users, including ICE agents and deportation officers, are members of a group called “Headspace_users.” Online therapy provider Headspace previously had an $82,500 federal contract with ICE that ended in 2023 to fund “mental health software required for ERO employees,” a reference to ICE’s deportation unit.

A spokesperson for Headspace said the company has not provided any services to DHS or ICE since 2023.

Dozens of other user groups reference Penlink , a web surveillance company that makes technology it claims can track the location data of hundreds of millions of mobile devices. Penlink has had a contract with ICE for years. The user groups vary in size, from a handful of users in local Homeland Security offices around the country to more than 2,000 users across ICE’s HSI unit nationally. One group specifically references Penlink PLX, which the company says is used to capture and analyze “real-time intelligence” from phone calls, texts, web activity, and social media.

A spokesperson for Penlink did not respond to a request for comment.

One user group also includes more than 200 CBP users associated with Mobile Fortify, a facial-recognition app used by both CBP and ICE agents to identify people and verify their information and immigration status .

items.title: Massive Leak Exposes 41,000 Homeland Security Workers—Including Undercover ICE Agents
items.summary: The leaked records include the locations of ICE and CBP facilities, workers’ cell phone numbers, and the members of groups tied to wiretap programs, Palantir software, and xAI’s Grok chatbot.
items.content:
An unprecedented leak of Department of Homeland Security records has exposed details of more than 41,000 employees or contractors who work for the department and its constituent agencies. The records include email addresses, phone numbers, and office addresses, but also references to internal systems and sensitive information on undercover and surveillance programs. In all, the leak provides a map of how DHS is organized and how it operates.

The records, which span DHS itself as well as seven component agencies, including Immigration and Customs Enforcement and US Customs and Border Protection, were last updated on August 19, 2026. The transparency nonprofit Distributed Denial of Secrets and cybersecurity researcher and journalist maia arson crimew previewed the data to WIRED, which they say they obtained from a group calling itself the Department of Peace.

DDoSecrets published the archive, which it calls "Icepick," on Wednesday. In a press release, DDoSecrets says the data is from DHS's Okta login system. In a note with the files, the hackers wrote, “They have our information, so it's only fair that we have theirs.”

An Okta spokesperson tells WIRED that it is unaware of any breach of its systems. “We are aware of this report. Okta is secure, and we have no evidence our data or systems were compromised,” the spokesperson says.

The leak comes as DHS has aggressively pursued its critics , seeking to unmask anonymous social media users, obtain customer records on protestors, and secure warrants for surveillance tools aimed at reporters. Since the start of the second Trump administration, DHS and the federal government have moved to hide DHS employees’ names and faces . The agency has also expanded its definition of “doxing”—a term that typically refers to publishing someone’s home address and other personal details for malicious purposes—to encompass the publication of basic facts about public employees, like their names and titles.

The leak follows a breach in which a group of hackers known as ShinyHunters claimed to have stolen personal information on nearly every FBI employee and their families. Law enforcement agencies have arrested several suspects and detained another who is alleged to be part of the group.

The DHS records are searchable on a website crimew built. “I don't think we should let them scare us into not looking into them,” she tells WIRED.

DHS and DOJ did not respond to WIRED’s request for comment. The FBI referred WIRED’s inquiry to DHS.

According to a WIRED analysis of the data, CBP staffers account for more than half of the records. ICE accounts for about 10,000, roughly a third of them in Homeland Security Investigations, ICE’s investigative wing. Another 6,200 belong to US Citizenship and Immigration Services, and nearly 1,000 are tied to the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, more than half of them contractors. Altogether, the files cover about a seventh of DHS’s workforce, revealing how DHS is structured, from senior leadership down to individual immigration agents and detention contractors.

Like most large organizations, DHS uses permission groups to control access to internal systems, according to the leaked records. Nearly everyone named in the leak has access to at least some of these systems. At HSI, 39 employees across more than a dozen field offices belong to groups whose names include “CUC,” which government court filings say stands for “certified undercover operation.” Another group, apparently based in HSI's St. Paul, Minnesota area of operations, references "Keyhole," which federal court filings describe as a certified undercover operation that recently funded HSI's undercover surveillance of Minneapolis protest groups earlier this year. Others reference a “Communications Intercept Center TechOps (CICTO) Program,” a “Title III Intercept Program” for wiretaps, and an “Illicit Sensor Intercept Program (ISIP).”

The names of the groups—there are over 55,000 in all—appear to reference tools for accessing immigration court records, pulling data from seized phones, and conducting surveillance. These include Palantir’s Falcon investigative platform and PenLink, which analyzes phone records and social media.

Two permission groups, named “Executive Leadership” and “AI Access,” appear to list people given exceptions to DHS's web filter, which blocks some websites for employees. They contain the same 13 people, including former DHS head Kristi Noem; Antoine McCord, the recently departed DHS chief information officer who has returned to defense tech company Anduril ; Philip Hegseth, listed as a senior advisor to the DHS secretary and the younger brother of defense secretary Pete Hegseth; and Jayce Krachenfels, listed as a policy adviser, who previously worked as a regional field director for Donald Trump’s 2024 presidential campaign, according to his LinkedIn profile.

Other groups named in the leak reference AI tools, including OpenAI’s ChatGPT, Google’s Gemini, and Microsoft’s Copilot. One, called “Grok.com,” includes eight DHS technology officials, including the department’s former chief information officer and chief data officer.

“If authentic and current, this is an extraordinarily valuable intelligence resource for those seeking to penetrate DHS,” says Alexander Leslie, a national security expert at the threat intelligence company Recorded Future. “This dataset becomes way more valuable when correlated with previously compromised information, commercial data, and other intelligence collections. An adversary could spend months exploiting these relationships to identify vulnerable personnel, develop convincing impersonation attempts, or compromise ongoing investigations.”

items.title: Anthropic just launched tools to show companies what their AI spending is buying
items.summary: The frontier lab is lifting the curtain on how users spend money on its models ahead of a planned IPO.
items.content:
The financials Anthropic shared with investors this week suggest that its AI coding tool, Claude Code, is every bit the business success the frontier lab wanted. The company recorded an operating profit in the second quarter, and 900% net revenue retention — that is, spending from the same customers in Q3 2025 grew nine times in Q3 2026.

Anthropic has focused on getting enterprise users to stick around and Wednesday announced a new suite of reporting tools designed to give those customers a more granular understanding of the value they get from their token spend.

Using internal analytics and employee surveys, managers can view a team’s work over a given date range, what the team produced, how much it cost, and where its workflows broke down. Anthropic says it won’t use this data for model training by default. The reports will also offer recommendations on how to improve the results.

This is a clear attempt to demonstrate the return on investment of Anthropic’s tools and to show customers how to improve it — a major concern among large customers. Anthropic is also creating pooled group budgets to allow teams to better manage token spending.

Businesses have been hunting for that kind of information as they figure out how best to deploy AI tools. While usage among venture-backed firms is driving token spend, most of the Fortune 500 are not seeing major gains from deploying AI.

Jellyfish, a company that makes tools for software developers, released a new report yesterday based on the use of agentic coding tools by 276,000 of its customers. Claude Code and other tools built on Anthropic models remain the most widely used in the survey, responsible for nearly a third of all proposed code changes submitted for review. More importantly, spending on those tools has grown 10x since the beginning of the year, with their cost now equal to about 2% of total engineering cost.

“Even if you’re saying 2% is still small, that 10x growth is growth that most CFOs didn’t plan for,” Nicholas Arcolano, the chief scientist at Jellyfish, told TechCrunch. We’re certainly getting to the point where people are realizing, okay, it’s not enough to just spend a bunch. You now have to optimize it, make it work.”

Anthropic’s new reports speak to that challenge. Anthropic leads among enterprise customers, but what makes an agentic coding tool truly sticky is difficult to identify. The release of OpenAI’s Astra model this summer seemed like a potential threat to Anthropic, but so far it hasn’t slowed Anthropic’s adoption numbers.

“It took a long time for us to see Codex really pop in our data at all, and it has come up with Astra [OpenAI’s latest model],” Nikolas Albarran, the AI product lead at Jellyfish, told TechCrunch. Looking at X, he continued, you’d get the distinct impression that the competition is more heated. “Everyone in the Valley is like, ‘Oh, Codex is better.’” In reality, Albarran continued, “Anthropic was just there with great enterprise motions, and they had an incumbent weight of their own — this stuff just worked and worked well, and a lot of people just put a lot of effort into standardizing workflows around it. And there’s not a big enough reason to switch.”

It’s not just a question of models and workflows, either. The realities of business mean that once a frontier lab has gotten its hooks into a customer, switching is harder than it is compared to an individual programmer or small organization. Albarran points to the investment all the major AI labs are making in forward-deployed engineering (FDE) organizations, teams that embed AI consultants inside customer organizations to help them get off the ground. These new reporting tools can be seen as a kind of FDE-lite, a lighter version of that hands-on help, for Anthropic customers.

“We’re at a point now where it’s mature enough, where once you’re in, it’s going to be harder and harder to switch because you’ve spent the effort,” he said. “Even if they’re all mostly the same, they’re all going to be slightly different, have their own slight quirks of how they handle agent.md files, etc., and so that cost to switch is not zero.”

We’ve gotten to play around with Apple’s next small tablet.

If you buy something from a link, The Verge may earn a commission. See our ethics statement.

Apple announced a new iPad Mini with a larger OLED display this week, and we’ve just gotten to try it out at Apple’s “Pro and tell” event.

It’s an iPad for sure, but the new OLED on the Mini looks exceptional, and the optional nano-texture matte finish is awesome. The “Pro and tell” event venue has soft lighting that’s not the most conducive to blinding glare on displays, but the matte finish pretty much squashes it entirely.

Moving the front-facing camera to the long edge is also a welcome change, matching other recent iPad models. (The shift means that the whole iPad line has the camera that way.) The reliance on Touch ID instead of Face ID is still a bummer, though.

The 8th-generation iPad Mini, revealed on Monday, has an 8.5-inch OLED screen, thinner bezels, and a higher peak brightness of up to 1,200 nits. The display still tops out at a 60Hz refresh rate instead of hitting 120Hz. It’s equipped with an A20 Pro chip, though the 128GB and 256GB models have five CPU cores , while the 512GB model gets six. Apple has also touted the new iPad Mini’s “Acoustic Display,” which includes woofers “paired through the display to produce punchier bass and more volume.”

The new iPad Mini starts at $699 and comes in two colors: starlight and midnight. It’s available to preorder now ahead of its launch on November 6th.

items.title: Touchscreen MacBook Pro hands-on: OLED looks great on a Mac
items.summary: It's not as different from the previous model as you might have expected.
items.content:
LOS ANGELES—For about five minutes on an extremely crowded showroom floor, I got to take pictures of the new MacBook Pro and test out some of its new features. First impressions: It’s not as much of a departure from the previous design as I expected, but the outstanding OLED display steals the show regardless.

The first thing I noticed was that it’s lighter. My daily driver is a 14-inch MacBook Pro (M1 Max), and it’s a bit weighty for a 14-incher. Picking up the new model, I could immediately tell it was lighter. It’s not like it’s in a different general weight class, but it’s a noticeable difference.

The next thing I noticed was the Dynamic Island. Given the larger screen real estate of a laptop, it’s much less dominant on the screen than it is on an iPhone. I do worry about what will happen with fullscreen games, which I wasn’t able to test today. The notch MacBook Pro has an option to maximize apps or games to just below the notch, so it doesn’t cut into the image. I’m curious to test in the full review whether that remains the case with this little cutout.

And lastly, the Apple logo on the back glows again! Some find this tacky, some find it essential. I just think it’s a little bit nostalgic.

Of course, you might make the case that the most notable thing about this laptop is not its weight or the Dynamic Island. For years, people have debated whether Apple should introduce a touchscreen laptop. Steve Jobs was famously against it. A few years ago—there were reports that under Tim Cook and now John Ternus—Apple decided to move ahead with the idea.

I played with it a bit, and it works just about exactly as you expect for a laptop touchscreen.

A few of the things I did with the touchscreen during my brief time with the laptop:

All of that is nice to have, I guess, but there’s not much you can do with it that you couldn’t already do with trackpad gestures, at least at the OS level; some creative apps, like finger painting on the screen, seemed to offer a bit more.

When the credible reports emerged that the MacBook Pro would get a touchscreen, I imagined a convertible with Apple Pencil support—something you could use as a large iPad or drawing tablet, essentially. That’s not what this is; it only takes the usual laptop shape, and I was told it does not support the Apple Pencil. It’s just a MacBook Pro, in its normal form factor, but you can use your fingers on the screen to do things like drag files around, swipe between desktop spaces, or pinch-to-zoom on maps or images.

But while it’s not about the touchscreen capability for me, I was impressed by the OLED screen itself—and I’m quite the display snob, if I’m being honest. The peak brightness, absolute blacks, well-balanced color, and dynamic range were genuinely remarkable. It’s an enormous upgrade over the MiniLED screen in the previous MacBook Pro.

It took far too long for OLED to come to the MacBook Pro, but unsurprisingly, Apple spared no expense and cut no immediately obvious corners on quality.

I was also happy to see that the cutout near the top of the screen that has replaced the camera notch is what Apple calls a Dynamic Island; it can resize to show live activities and other information on the fly. That’s one of my favorite features on the iPhone, as I’ve been impressed with Apple’s ability to turn something that should be an albatross into an appealing feature.

Based on my time with the device and today’s announcement, the screen seems to be the main draw (though it’s nice that it noticeably weighs less, too), but the price is the real barrier. A 16-inch model with an M5 Max, 64 GB of RAM, and 2 TB of storage is currently priced at $5,799. Sure, that’s a high-end spec, but that’s some serious cash. Much of that is due to the storage and memory; upgrading from 64GB to 128GB adds a whopping $1,600 to that.

Sure, most people don’t need anywhere near that much RAM—but some might for future-proofing for local AI workflows.

I’m looking forward to spending more time with the new MacBook Pro, but for right now, it seems to follow in the lineup’s existing tradition: impressively high-end components like an outstanding OLED panel, but a very steep price to match. No surprises here! Though after well over a decade of speculation and back-and-forth, you’d be forgiven for being surprised that the touchscreen thing actually finally happened.

items.title: The New M6 MacBook Pro Has a Serious Price Problem
items.summary: For $1,999, you could own an M6 Mac Mini and an M5 MacBook Air instead, both of which are on sale right now.
items.content:
Just yesterday, Apple refreshed its 14-inch MacBook Pro with the new M6 chip inside, and it’s currently available for preorder . This is the first MacBook to get the chip (but certainly not the last), and I look forward to testing this thing out myself. But I do already have a good sense of how well it’ll perform, as I already tested this same chip in the latest Mac Mini . And it points to an issue with the current state of the Mac lineup .

The 14-inch M6 MacBook Pro currently costs $1,999. That gets you 16 GB of RAM and 512 GB of storage. Even for as good as these laptops are, that feels like too much money for those specs. Apple raised prices across all Macs earlier this year, but the base 14-inch MacBook Pro got hit the hardest, with a $300 bump. It was already an awkward configuration, as it used the same M5 chip as the much cheaper MacBook Air models. It was such bad pricing that it ended up on my “do not buy” list. The addition of the M6 seems like it’ll add some value, especially with the improvements to GPU performance I saw in the M6 Mac Mini. It also has the dual Neural Engine, which can speed up certain AI tasks in creative applications, especially for content creators. I won’t pretend to make a final evaluation until I’ve thoroughly tested the machine myself.

But consider this. The M6 Mac Mini is on sale for $779 right now, $120 off its retail price. The 13-inch M5 MacBook Air is similarly $150 off its retail price right now. You could buy both for the same price as one M6 MacBook Pro. That’s kind of insane when you think about it. You miss out on the MacBook Pro’s excellent Mini-LED display and powerful speakers, but to me, it’s a tempting alternative for a $2,000 budget.

It’s even more compelling when you consider how many people are using Mac Minis these days—more as always-on AI agent boxes that you can control remotely with any old MacBook. Pairing the M6 Mac Mini and M5 MacBook air together is a recipe for AI goodness (especially if you configure the Mac Mini up to 32 GB or 64 GB of memory).

Another alternative is the M5 MacBook Pro with an M5 Pro chip inside for only $200 more. It looks identical on the outside, and has better performance on the inside.

I’m still interested to see how the new M6 MacBook Pro performs, but the price alone makes me wonder if there aren’t better ways of spending your money—even while staying within the Mac lineup.

items.title: Google announces Gemini 4 Carbon, its latest frontier AI model that you can't use
items.summary: Gemini 4 Carbon is essentially a slightly better version of Argon.
items.content:
It’s almost like Google’s got something to prove after taking a break from releasing new frontier AI models earlier this year. Just two weeks after rolling out Gemini 4 Argon , Google has announced Gemini 4 Carbon . This isn’t the Flash model equivalent we’ve been waiting for but, rather, is an improvement on Argon, and like that model, Google is working on a staged release that could take a while.

Stop me if you’ve heard this one before: Google says its latest AI model reaches a new threshold in coding, agentic tasks, and scientific analysis. It’s so capable, in fact, that Google can’t let you use it just yet.

Gemini 4 Carbon reportedly makes big gains in cybersecurity applications. Google says the model shows a “significant leap” in vulnerability detection, validation, and remediation. Carbon is also apparently twice as likely to generate code that is free of vulnerabilities versus Argon. Meanwhile, the Chrome team claims that Carbon is 10 times better at generating “high-quality” patches compared to non-Google models. Google also notes that Carbon has increased its score by 89 points on WebDev Arena , now ranking at number four on the leaderboard.

Google has some numbers to support these vague assessments (below), showing Carbon at the top of the charts. Google positions Carbon as a totally new model, but for all we know, it could be a post-training upgrade of Argon. The two models have a lot in common, but Carbon does best Argon by slim margins in every test Google has given it. Its new model also beats GPT-6 Astra, Claude Opus 5.5, and Claude Fable 5.1 in almost every test. Benchmarks don’t tell the whole story, of course, and it’s notable that every frontier model scores in the same neighborhood in these tests. The gap between Carbon and the competition is just a few points.

Credit: Google Credit: Google

By Google’s reckoning, Carbon is the most capable frontier AI model right now, and its improved capabilities come with more rigorous safeguards. In the Grey Swan evaluation, Carbon resisted every attempted prompt-injection attack. That 0 percent score is better than Argon (0.7 percent), Opus 5.5 (1 percent), and GPT-6 Astra (8.5 percent).

The release plans for Gemini 4 Carbon mirror those for Argon. According to Google, the model’s strong performance in agentic coding and cybersecurity means that it has to take a “deliberative approach.” The company is working within the voluntary testing framework established by the US government, and it plans to roll the model out through its Fairwinds cyber defense program once that’s done. Google does not make any promises about the timeline for a wide release of Gemini 4 Carbon, but if it’s anything like Argon, the model could be available in a couple of weeks .

items.title: I Put a Bunch of AI Agents in Charge of a Fantasy Soccer Team. They’re Not Better Than Humans—Yet
items.summary: To experiment with AI’s predictive skills, I let Codex loose on a fantasy team. It tried to bench Erling Haaland at first, but it soon learned the error of its ways.
items.content:
I have consulted my AI-powered crystal ball, and it’s telling me that frontier models are going to get a lot better at making predictions in the near future. Just ask my Premier League fantasy team .

A few weeks ago, I deployed a small horde of AI agents to craft and manage an experimental roster. Given the proliferation of AI agents into pretty much every aspect of our lives, I wanted to know if a swarm of bots could put together a winning team.

I first looked at the potential for AI here a few years ago, playing around with a tool from the UK’s Turing Institute that selected teams after modeling previous fantasy league data. Its suggestions were remarkably bonkers—it didn’t incorporate real-world information, like a player’s injury or a team’s change in management.

This time, while on a flight to visit family, I asked Codex for help. First, I fed the model a couple of relevant research papers. Then, I asked it to build a harness—instructions and code that guides different agents through various steps—that would check recent news and run a model to make predictions.

It quickly came up with a setup that seemed to collate and analyze way more information than I ever would have. And yet I was surprised by how dumb the initial team suggestions were. Leaving Erling Haaland on the bench? Really, Codex?

I then asked Codex to create a team of agents that did different things: several that read news and blog posts; others that analyzed recent results; more that ran models; and a bunch that critiqued suggestions. This seemed to significantly improve the suggestions. I tried increasing the number of agents to more than 100, hoping this would make the system smarter still, but it didn’t change much besides running up my API bill.

Still, the improvement from a few years ago was striking. According to Haifeng Xu , a computer scientist at the University of Chicago who studies the uses of AI in market situations, newer models may be even better at making predictions because they’re able to consume and analyze huge amounts of real-world information, and they’re able to orchestrate more complex systems for their guesses.

“AI is just getting smarter in understanding the world—I feel like that's the fundamental reason they’re improving,” Xu tells me.

Late last year, Xu was marveling at the growing popularity of prediction markets like Kalshi and Polymarket . He wondered how the best commercial models might fare on those markets, so alongside several colleagues, he began testing their forecasting skills.

They had models guess, for example, who would win the NBA Championship and who President Trump would meet with.

“Very quickly we started to realize that models did really well,” Xu tells me. The models were sometimes able to do better than the average person without any special instructions or guidance, he says. In their testing, GPT-5 was the best at making predictions, followed by Grok 4, Claude Sonnet, Gemini, and Llama.

The team went on to develop Prophet Arena , a benchmark that measures a model’s ability to make predictions. It’s one of a number of benchmarks designed to test AI’s future-gazing capabilities; another, Prediction Arena , from researchers at Harvard University and a company called Arcada Labs, recently gave frontier models $10,000 to wager on prediction markets over 57 days. The models consistently lost money in their experiment, but the researchers saw evidence of them improving consistently over time.

Xu tells me that AI can most effectively make predictions using a custom harness, and notes that having agents with unique tasks—reading the news, collecting other data, and analyzing the whole system, for instance—seems to be the most effective approach.

Interestingly, AI still often lags behind very skilled experts known as superforecasters. Xu explains that, although humans cannot consume as much information, their understanding of the real world—that is, of the dynamics behind a news story—is deeper.

That said, there’s growing evidence that the human superforecaster’s edge is eroding. A contest called the Metaculus Cup recently showed that AI can sometimes beat even the best human predictors. And a benchmark called ForecastBench could provide further evidence that AI can match human skills when the results of an ongoing contest conclude soon. In fact, I think we can expect the big labs to turn their attention to future-gazing as a powerful new way to measure progress in machine intelligence.

All of these predictive experiments seem to suggest that, like math, coding, and law, industries predicated on trading may soon be upended by AI. Perhaps the best human traders will take on a new kind of role: supervising and orchestrating AI agents capable of divining the future far better than they can.

For the time being, my AI’s suggestions still don’t seem all that impressive. Its team hasn’t outscored the average over the past weeks. I certainly won’t be using any of its suggestions in my own selections.

But AI will no doubt get better, perhaps making it all too easy to dominate fantasy league pretty soon. I’m kind of hoping it won’t, though, as it would spoil the fun of trying to earn bragging rights by winning all by yourself.
