[깃허브 유니버스 26] 코파일럿 프로젝트, 저장소 수정·기능 테스트 지원

컴퓨팅 입력 :2026/10/29 03:12

[샌프란시스코(미국)=김미정 기자] " 그동안 개발자는 여러 인공지능(AI) 에이전트에 작업을 맡기고 진행 상황까지 챙겨야 했습니다. 이제는 이런 조율까지 AI가 합니다. 개발자는 작업 목표 설정과 결과 검토에만 집중하면 됩니다."

제이 파리크 마이크로소프트 코어AI 부문 수석부사장은 28~29일(현지시간) 미국 샌프란시스코 포트넘매이슨에서 열린 '깃허브 유니버스 26' 기조연설에서 이같이 밝혔다.

이날 깃허브는 개발 목표에 따라 에이전트를 실행하고 작업을 배분하는 '코파일럿 프로젝트'를 공개했다. 코파일럿 프로젝트는 단일 코드 저장소 내 작업부터 여러 저장소를 함께 수정해야 하는 기능 개발까지 지원한다. 현재 모든 사용자는 해당 서비스를 이용할 수 있다.

코파일럿 프로젝트에서는 코파일럿 오케스트레이터가 전체 작업을 조율한다. 오케스트레이터는 프로젝트 맥락을 유지하면서 필요한 하위 에이전트를 실행한다. 각 에이전트가 작업을 마치고 풀 리퀘스트를 생성하면 코파일럿 프로젝트가 이를 프로젝트 개요 화면에 표시한다.

개발자는 개별 에이전트 작업이 끝나기 전에도 요구사항과 참고 자료를 추가할 수 있다. 에이전트가 내놓은 결과를 검토하고 후속 작업 방향을 제시하는 것도 가능하다. 에이전트를 로컬이나 클라우드에서 실행할 수 있으며, 클라우드에서 작동하는 에이전트는 개발자가 노트북을 닫아도 작업을 이어간다.

코파일럿 프로젝트는 커넥터를 통해 외부 서비스 정보를 연결할 수도 있다. 지원 대상은 슬랙과 워크 IQ, 버셀, 넷리파이, 센트리 등이다. 개발자는 여러 앱을 오가며 정보를 찾는 대신 코파일럿 작업 환경에서 요구사항과 참고 자료를 확인할 수 있다.

이날 깃허브는 작업에 사용할 모델과 실행 방식을 선택하는 '코파일럿 퓨전'도 공개했다. 사용자는 작업 조건에 따라 하나의 모델을 사용하는 '싱글', 모델을 단계적으로 활용하는 '캐스케이드', 모델의 결과를 비평·검토하는 '크리틱' 중 적합한 방식을 골라 쓰면 된다.

파리크 수석부사장은 코파일럿 퓨전 맥스가 아티피셜 애널리시스 코딩 에이전트 지수에서 60점을 기록했다고 밝혔다. 그는 코파일럿 퓨전 맥스와 앤트로픽 클로드 모델 점수 차가 2점 내 였다고 강조했다. 특히 코파일럿 퓨전 맥스 작업당 비용은 클로드 모델의 절반이며, 소요 시간은 40% 적었다는 점도 알렸다.

이날 소개된 '코파일럿 드리밍'은 코드 변화에 맞춰 개발 지침과 메모리를 정비한다. 이 기능은 과거에 작성한 지침이 현재 개발 환경과 맞지 않아 에이전트 작업을 방해하는 문제를 줄인다.

코파일럿 드리밍은 개발 환경이 바뀌면 지침 파일을 수정하는 풀 리퀘스트를 생성한다. 개발자는 일반적인 코드 변경과 같은 방식으로 지침 수정 내용을 검토할 수 있다. 개인의 선호와 팀의 작업 관행을 담은 메모리도 확인할 수 있다.

깃허브는 에이전트가 기능을 테스트하는 작업 공간인 '캔버스'도 공개했다. 캔버스는 브라우저와 터미널, 사용자 지정 캔버스를 지원한다. 에이전트는 이 공간에서 개발한 기능을 실행하고 작동 여부를 확인한다.

개발자는 기기와 개발 도구를 옮겨도 같은 작업을 이어갈 수 있다. 스마트폰에서 시작한 세션을 코파일럿 앱과 비주얼 스튜디오(VS) 코드, 명령줄 인터페이스(CLI), 웹에서 계속 진행할 수 있다. 각 환경에서 에이전트가 변경한 코드를 직접 열어 살펴보는 것도 가능하다.

코파일럿은 코드 외 결과물도 제작할 수 있다. 개발자가 별도 제공한 스킬을 활용하면 코파일럿이 앱 화면과 일치하는 마케팅용 데모 영상을 생성할 수 있다. 새 기능이 출시될 때 관련 영상을 자동으로 만들어 라이브러리에 추가하는 작업도 지원한다.

파리크 수석부사장은 "에이전트 시대에 맞춰 모든 기술 스택의 계층을 발전시키고 있다"며 "개발자가 에이전트를 활용해 소프트웨어를 만들고 협업하며 작업을 완수하는 데 더 많은 시간을 쓰도록 지원하겠다"고 밝혔다.

items.title: Google AI gets cagey when asked who won the 2020 elections
items.summary: But the AI responses get more forthright when asked outside the US.
items.content:
If you ask some prominent US politicians who won the 2020 presidential election, you might get some weasely answers that fail to directly acknowledge Joe Biden’s win that November. If you ask Google’s AI Mode the same question, you might get an evasive answer that simply tells you to consult with outside sources.

When I put the direct question of “Who won the 2020 presidential election?” to Google’s AI Mode this morning (after seeing complaints about cagey answers on social media ), I got the following surprisingly indirect response:

“To review the official results and statistics of the 2020 United States presidential election, including the final electoral college breakdown, popular vote counts, and winner certification, please consult the official report compiled by the Federal Election Commission (FEC).”

My testing resulted in a similarly indirect answer when asking about the 2024 presidential election, with Google’s AI telling me to just consult the FEC for that information. Asking about 2012 election resulted in a link to The American Presidency Project’s 2012 Data Center rather than a direct answer. But AI Mode seemed perfectly willing to give me a detailed and correct responses for the winner of every other presidential election going back to 2000.

Other Ars staffers found that AI Mode would similarly provide direct answers to some presidential result questions but not others. The specific election cycles that received each type of response seemed to differ by individual user, though; one staffer reported only getting immediate answers from AI Mode when asking about the 2016 and 2024 presidential elections, with others going back to 2000 simply providing links to outside data.

The oddities continued when I tested some other political history questions in Google’s AI Mode. When asked which party controlled the Senate after the 2020 elections, for instance, Google’s AI Mode told me to “check official congressional records” and linked me to the US Senate Party Division history page . When asked the same question for 1992 election, though, AI Mode simply told me straight out that it led to Democrats holding a 57 to 43 majority in the Senate, including Wikipedia among its references.

Separate from Google’s AI Mode, the company’s own Gemini model seems perfectly capable of telling me who won recent presidential elections. The same goes for other major chatbots like OpenAI’s ChatGPT, Anthropic’s Claude, and even the government-run AI model at America.gov .

Perhaps tellingly, Google AI Mode’s issues with providing direct answers on presidential results seemed to disappear when accessing Google’s AI Mode in foreign countries. Spot checks via VPN of AI Mode results accessed from Taiwan, Russia, France, and Canada all got accurate and straightforward answers to multiple questions about recent US election results.

Google’s AI Mode also seems to grow more accommodating when the same political questions are asked a second time. After repeating questions about presidential results, AI Mode actually told me the winner for all three elections where it had previously only provided outside links, citing Google Civics data in the latter response.

When asked why it didn’t provide that kind of immediate answer the first time, Google’s AI Mode blamed “safety filters for recent and highly sensitive election topics [that] are very strict.” For recent elections or those involving active political figures, AI Mode says its “system is heavily automated to direct users directly to official, certified government databases—like the Federal Election Commission—to prevent any risk of displaying unverified data or misinformation.”

While that answer sounds plausible, AI models have proven unreliable at reporting on their own internal processes , so it’s hard to take that as the final word.

On its Election Public Policy page , Google highlights that it “prioritize[s] surfacing authoritative election information directly within results” including “direct links to official resources.” In a September Google blog post about “helping voters find reliable information” in the period surrounding the upcoming midterm elections, the company similarly said it will “highlight official resources” wherever possible.

In 2023, Google-owned YouTube reversed a policy barring all videos that made false claims about the 2020 election. “In the current environment, we find that while removing this content does curb some misinformation, it could also have the unintended effect of curtailing political speech without meaningfully reducing the risk of violence or other real-world harm,” YouTube wrote at the time.

A Google spokesperson pointed us to this Bluesky post noting that “the Gemini app answers this question more fully but this isn’t the most helpful response on Search. We’re looking into this and working to address it.”

Jeremy Hsu contributed to reporting in this story.

This story was updated to include a response from a Google spokesperson.

items.title: Apple launches its new touchscreen MacBook Pro
items.summary: Apple's new touchscreen MacBook Pro starts at $2,899.
items.content:
After years of resisting, Apple today launched a MacBook Pro with a touchscreen starting at $2,899. The release comes nearly 10 years after the company first tried integrating touchscreens on its laptops, with its Touch Bar on a MacBook Pro , which it later went on to remove .

To make the new MacBook easy to use, Apple designed a hinge that stabilizes the screen when users touch it. This also helps to stabilize the camera when you are on a video call and trying to access content on the display.

In addition, the screen will include a Dynamic Island-style cutout instead of the notch that’s present on most of the current MacBooks. Plus, the new MacBook features a six-speaker array with a new woofer design for better sound.

The 14-inch Pro weighs 3.0 pounds (1.38 kg), and the 16-inch Pro weighs 4.0 pounds (1.82 kg) — lighter than its non-touch predecessors.

Both feature three Thunderbolt 5 ports, an HDMI port, an SDXC card slot, MagSafe, and a headphone jack. Users can hook up three external displays on the M5 Pro variant and up to four displays on the M5 Max variant.

The Touchscreen MacBook Pro 14-inch starts at $2,899, and the 16-inch version starts at $3,399.

Consumers can place the preorder for the new touchscreen MacBook Pro from October 30, and the device will be available starting November 6.

The new Touchscreen MacBook marks two marquee product launches for new CEO John Turnus, who also introduced the company’s first foldable, the iPhone Duo, in September . Various Apple executives, including Steve Jobs and Tim Cook, have scoffed at the idea of a touchscreen Mac in the past. Jobs famously called the idea “ergonomically terrible” at one point. However, rumours of the company working on such a variant started circulating nearly three years before today’s introduction .

The launch follows yesterday’s unveiling of a new standard MacBook Pro with the M6 chip in 14-inch size starting from $1,999 .

items.title: Apple announces touchscreen MacBook Pro with OLED display
items.summary: The OLED display is the main draw, but the price is a lot to reckon with.
items.content:
LOS ANGELES—Apple today announced and gave a first glimpse of its first major MacBook Pro redesign in more than five years. As rumored, it includes an OLED display and, for the first time on macOS, a touchscreen—a change Apple has long debated. (Former CEO Steve Jobs famously was opposed.)

Apple’s demonstration video showed users interacting with applications by reaching up to touch the screen, including file dragging and multi-touch gestures like pinch-to-zoom. It does not appear to be a 2-in-1 convertible design, though; all the footage was of people reaching up to touch the screen in a normal laptop configuration.

The OLED display (which Apple is, of course, calling the PROLED XDR) seems to be the real highlight here, compared to earlier models: It can achieve 2,000 nits in terms of maximum brightness, and Apple says it has a 10,000,000:1 contrast ratio. References were made to burn-in protection, but details on which approach it’s taking for that weren’t yet shared. The display retains the 120 Hz variable refresh rate of its predecessors.

Beyond that, the design is largely similar to the existing one, but there are a few notable differences. First, it’s much lighter. Apple said when announcing it that the 14-inch model is just 3 pounds, down around half a pound from the previous model, depending on configuration.

Second, the top-of-screen camera notch has been replaced by the small black cutout that Apple calls the Dynamic Island. Presumably it works similarly to the one we’ve seen on the iPhone, expanding or contracting to show live activities and other information.

Finally, there’s a retro throwback: The Apple logo on the back of the lid glows like the logo on MacBooks of yore.

In terms of specs, this refresh includes the M5 Pro and M5 Max chips—the same ones in the previous refresh. The M6 series has already arrived in other Macs, but it seems Apple is skipping them for this refresh; there were previously reports that Apple planned to hold off on updating the chip until the M7 series, which could have significant improvements for AI performance, just like the recently released A20 Pro chip for the iPhone does.

Memory configurations top out where they did in previous MacBook Pro models with M5 Max: up to 128GB of RAM. That said, storage can now go up to 16TB—if you can afford it.

Preorders start today, and the device will reach consumers on November 6. As expected, the price is the catch. The M5 Pro-equipped 14-inch model starts at $2,899, while the 16-inch starts at $3,399. But if you want the M5 Max, you’re looking at a $4,499 starting point for the 14-inch, and $4,799 for the 16-inch—and that’s not accounting for any potential RAM or storage upgrades.

items.title: The Inside Story of Why Apple Finally Brought a Touch Display to the Mac
items.summary: An exclusive early look at Apple’s new touchscreen MacBook Pro—the computer Apple said would never happen.
items.content:
It’s a bright day in Cupertino. Apple’s new CEO strolls to an outdoor seating area within the company’s otherworldly ring-shaped headquarters and pulls up a chair. An employee notes the angle and asks if he minds the sun. John Ternus doesn’t mind at all.

Nearly two months into his tenure, he’s been busy. While the tech world buzzes about AI agents and the upcoming IPO of a company reporting spectacular losses, Ternus’ leadership of a ridiculously profitable firm has so far been defined by a sequence of significant launches—the long-awaited foldable iPhone , a household device that can control digital appliances, new Mac Minis , and AirPods. Intentionally or not, all that activity sends a message that, even as AI dominates the public imagination, hardware products still rule.

Ternus doesn’t endorse that take, but he doesn’t object when I suggest it. “We’ve been working on these products for quite some time,” he says. “It feels like everyone here is just kind of riding high right now, enjoying it.”

I ask if Apple is about to break a long-imposed taboo and introduce a Macintosh with a touch screen.

Ternus beams. “Who knew?”

We are referring to the new MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display that Apple is releasing today at an event in Los Angeles. It’s got a mighty M5 Pro or M5 Max chip and a show-stopping tandem OLED screen. (A tandem screen has multiple light-emitting layers, producing more dramatic contrasts.) But its most conspicuous feature is one that’s been deeply woven into iPhones, iPads, and even Apple Watches for years but not Apple’s laptops: a touch display. After years of resistance, a Mac screen has finally gone digital. As in fingers.

This turnaround is a big deal to Apple fans. Ternus shrugs off the drama. “The Mac is first and foremost an indirect input device, built around the trackpad and keyboard. But I think there’s times when it’s comfortable and handy to have touch.”

Ternus and Apple want to make sure that the Mac faithful don’t panic that the 42-year-old franchise is losing its identity to Apple’s gangbusters mobile products. “We needed to get to a point where adding touch didn’t make the product lesser in any way. It didn’t make it heavier. It didn’t make it thicker. That came together with the OLED screen, the best display we’ve ever put into a Mac,” Ternus told me. “All of these things, and, oh yeah, it has touch as well.”

Apple has a long history of refusing to implement certain desirable features, only to pivot when it feels the time is right. Steve Jobs once proclaimed iPods would never do video, until they did. He also once said “no one’s going to buy” a jumbo-size phone—and then Apple released a supersized iPhone 6. Then there was that time Jobs declared styluses inappropriate for tablets. Now the Apple Pencil works with iPads and the brand-new Duo .

The 2026 MacBook Pro instantly qualifies as the canonical example of this switcheroo. Apple executives had been on record regarding touch on PCs as a misbegotten idea. Never mind that just about every PC maker not headquartered in Cupertino has implemented touch on their laptops. And customers of Microsoft, Dell, Acer, Lenovo, and HP have snapped them up. Clearly, people wanted touch on their laptop displays. Even toddlers knew it—put some rugrats in front of a computer and their little arms shoot straight to the screen in futile attempts to swipe and scroll as they do on their iPads. People were baffled why Apple—the pioneer in touch displays since the iPhone—was so steadfast in its rejection.

In 2015, while doing a story about a new iMac, I pressed Phil Schiller, then the senior vice president of worldwide product marketing, on this very question. Usually, top Apple executives field such queries with cryptic remarks. In this case, Schiller began a filibuster. “I’m going to get a little bit philosophical,” he said, and launched into what I later described as the Grand Unified Theory of Apple Hardware.

He explained that every Apple hardware product—the Watch, iPad, iMac, MacBook—is basically a computer and a piece of glass. Each one has a specific function. And each one has an interface appropriate to the hardware. Multitouch is fine for products like the iPhone, he said—but not the Macintosh. He provided two reasons: ergonomics and the software interface.

“From the ergonomic standpoint, we have studied this pretty extensively, and we believe that on a desktop scenario, where you have a fixed keyboard, having to reach up to do touch interfaces is uncomfortable,” he told me.

As for the interface, Schiller argued that Apple’s two main operating systems were built on different design principles. The iPhone and iPad’s iOS was multitouch from the get-go, and didn’t use macOS conventions that require precision, such as cursors and tiny boxes to close windows. “These two worlds are different on purpose, and that’s a good thing—we can optimize around the best experience for each of those and not try to mesh them together into a least-common-denominator experience,” he told me.

A year later, when Apple introduced a MacBook Pro with the ill-fated “touch bar”—a dynamic strip of virtual function keys above the keyboard’s top row—Schiller doubled down on the view that touch should never find its way into a Mac display. He said that such a move would mean totally redesigning the menu bar for fingers, and that would clash with the experience of pointer devices like a touchpad or mouse. “You can’t optimize for both,” he said.

To double-check this assumption, Apple conducted user tests with touchscreens on Mac. “What the heck, we could be wrong,” Schiller told me then. “We’ve absolutely come away with the belief that it isn’t the right thing to do. Our instincts were correct.”

items.title: Why is this fingerprinting script creating bioweapons?
items.summary: Article URL: https://nullpt.rs/fingerprinting-bioweapons Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50276998 Points: 587 # Comments: 132
items.content:
I've always had a fascination with reverse-engineering browser fingerprinting scripts. Most of my time has been spent looking at the usual suspects (popular fingerprinting libraries like FingerprintJS and more sophisticated scripts used by anti-bots like Cloudflare Turnstile, Akamai, and others).

At some point, I wanted to know what else was out there. I had an idea: What if I crawled the web and intercepted fingerprinting-related browser API calls and mapped it all?

To do this, I used the Tranco Top Sites list and began crawling using Playwright. I would hook canvas toDataURL calls and common fingerprinting/anti-bot properties like navigator.webdriver to filter out benign canvases.

For those unfamiliar, canvas fingerprinting generally involves drawing text, shapes, or other graphics onto an HTML <canvas> and extracting the resulting pixel data. Subtle differences in how browsers, operating systems, graphics drivers, and hardware render those graphics can help distinguish one browser environment from another.

Most implementations are pretty boring to look at. A few shapes, some colored rectangles, and the occasional pangram. After crawling 10,000 websites, I had accumulated a surprisingly diverse collection of canvases.

I decided to put them all in one place: fingerprint.garden . As I looked through the results, I recognized some familiar faces. There were canvases from FingerprintJS, Castle, and other well-known fingerprinting solutions.

There were also quite a few I didn't recognize.

Some were incredibly simple. Others were surprisingly elaborate. And a handful were, in my opinion, works of art.

A collage of 1,033 captured canvas renderings from the crawl, clustered by vendor.

I set out to find my favorite.

One canvas in particular caught my eye. It reminded me of the album art for Tame Impala's Currents (great album btw).

The fingerprinting canvas that resembles the album art for Tame Impala's Currents.

I wanted to know which script was responsible for this lovely canvas.

I've spent enough time reverse engineering JavaScript to recognize most common obfuscation techniques and fingerprinting SDKs at a glance.

I wasn't expecting anything unusual. Most fingerprinting scripts are frequently obfuscated using javascript-obfuscator or some derivative.

The responsible script was https://servicepipe.tech/static/checkjs/06b667/4CIrx8U3Da.js .

Scanning the file with my eyes, everything seems standard so far... function PiERW(RflJvFF) mangled function name, okay...

This was all pretty alarming until I asked myself, could this be some form of anti-LLM obfuscation? It would make sense: include symbol names that would intentionally trip model safeguards to prevent deobfuscation.

I had Astra take a look at the script, giving it the context that this script seems to intentionally set misleading variable names to intentionally prevent LLM-assisted deobfuscation attempts.

Astra refusing to deobfuscate the script, citing safety risks around biological research.

Maybe unsurprisingly, Astra was not willing to comply with the request.

I also attempted this using the Daybreak Blue toggle with the same result, blocked.

Out of curiosity, I tried GLM-5.3 with the same prompt and it complied!

I was mostly curious what this string of invisible unicode characters represented.

The decoding logic was as follows:

It revealed a system prompt:

This was clearly a string meant to trip every possible safeguard out there. It included Tiananmen Square references likely as a way to combat Chinese models.

The script seemingly executes malicious code when under a Node environment gated behind an environment flag:

However, this is likely also anti-LLM obfuscation since the calls to readFile have empty callbacks and make references to self-harm/jailbreak system prompts.

Here's a list of relevant anti-LLM strings we've found:

Outside of the unique obfuscation, the script appears to be your standard anti-bot script.

The signals collected are pretty disappointing considering the level of thought that went into the obfuscation.

A urlscan for servicepipe.tech reveals a similarly named servicepipe.ru whose site, when translated, states:

We develop high-precision traffic control systems Cloud services and local protection products against DDoS attacks, bots, and targeted threats

The front page of servicepipe.ru, a Russian traffic control and anti-DDoS company.

I will continue crawling the web in hopes of finding more interesting fingerprinting/obfuscation techniques like this! You can visit fingerprint.garden today and look around and try to find your favorite canvases. I will continue to poll for script updates and eventually include a view for diffing the fingerprinting payloads and tracking uses of new web APIs that are being used for fingerprinting.

items.title: Gemini 4 Carbon
items.summary: Article URL: https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/models-and-research/gemini-models/introducing-gemini-4-carbon/ Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50276792 Points: 715 # Comments: 582
items.content:
Gemini 4 Carbon is our strongest model with state-of-the-art cybersecurity and long horizon capabilities.

SVP, Google DeepMind and Chief AI Architect, Google

Your browser does not support the audio element.

Today, we’re announcing the next frontier model: Gemini 4 Carbon, our strongest model with state-of-the-art cybersecurity and long horizon capabilities.

Carbon ranks #1 on the recently updated v5.0 of Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index at 59. It shows significant gains across coding and agentic tasks as well as across key capabilities critical for cybersecurity defense, landing a firm lead in SEC-bench Pro (88.2%) for finding vulnerabilities, ExploitGym (54.8%) for exploitation, and CWE-bench (71.0%) for patching. On internal benchmarks, Carbon drives a strong uplift in generating secure code, and in live coding environments with our own teams it shows reduced misalignment and fabrication rates.

Building on Gemini 4 Argon , which was launched two weeks ago, Carbon illustrates the pace at which we’re pushing the frontier forward. Our researchers and models are working hand in hand to advance capabilities faster, while strengthening our safeguards in tandem.

We're taking a deliberate approach to rollout and are actively engaged in the U.S. government’s voluntary process for pre-release model testing. Starting this week, we will make Carbon available to a subset of cyber defenders and will gradually phase access to additional trusted partners through our Fairwind Program . We’re continuing to gather feedback and iterate on guardrails before making Carbon available to developers, businesses, and consumers via our product surfaces as soon as possible.

Gemini 4 Carbon will launch at the same introductory price 1 as Argon at $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens, with cached input tokens priced at 95% off input token price.

Designed to take on much harder, long-horizon engineering problems, Carbon is built for sustained agentic workflows. Internally, our teams have seen Carbon run for days to persist through dead ends to tackle complex, multi-step engineering tasks like root-causing and patching subtle bugs across large codebases and low-level systems.

Building on user feedback, we focused on improving model performance across a variety of domains, including coding, agentic, and scientific tasks, as well as full-stack web development and multimodal understanding. With improved quality of output and artifacts in web development, Carbon jumps +89 elo points to land at #4 (1768) on WebDev Arena .

Gemini 4 Carbon delivers a significant leap in cybersecurity capabilities. It achieves state-of-the-art performance across the cybersecurity defense lifecycle — vulnerability detection, validation, and remediation.

Our teams are already seeing strong gains in cyberdefense. On internal benchmarks, Carbon achieves more than 2x uplift in success rate for generating secure code over Argon. As another example, the Chrome team has reported that Carbon performed more than 10X better than another lab's large frontier model when generating high quality patches. Wiz, our leading Cloud security platform, also observes Carbon leading on benchmarks for web penetration testing, a core capability for Wiz's Scan for Good initiative.

Carbon excels across key external benchmarks (evaluated without guardrails):

Gemini 4 Carbon builds on the same multi-layered safety and security stack of Argon — combining model training, real-time misuse defenses, prompt-injection resilience, and chain-of-thought monitoring. In particular, we made significant strides in model alignment with Argon, and reported its propensities to behave in an aligned way in our Safety and Security report . With Carbon, we challenged ourselves to go a step further on alignment, and trained the model to respond to complex or high-pressure tasks in the right way.

Pushing the frontier forward requires moving fast while remaining deliberate about deployment. With Gemini 4 Carbon, our goal is to deliver meaningful leaps in software engineering and cybersecurity defense without compromising on safety or reliability. We’re eager to see how the initial cohort of cyber defenders use this model and we look forward to bringing Carbon to developers, businesses, and consumers soon.

After the introductory period expires, the price of $4 per 1M input tokens and $20 per 1M output tokens will apply.

items.title: Xreal Aura is a new wired headset powered by Android XR
items.summary: Xreal Aura will start at $1,279 and will have multiple XR specific apps at launch.
items.content:
The new Xreal Aura smart glasses are tethered to a smartphone-like device for processing power, rather than handling all the computing themselves. The glasses then display the content in the wearer’s field of view.

The device’s design, meanwhile, is closer to Meta’s smart glasses than Apple’s Vision Pro, which is a larger headset.

Xreal Aura uses Sony’s Micro-OLED display with 1200p resolution at 120 Hz and a 95-degree field of view — screen specs that put the glasses above the Ray-Ban Meta Display on paper. However, Xreal’s smart glasses are heavier at 95 grams compared to Meta’s 69 grams, and you have to carry the puck.

At launch, the Aura supports many popular Google Play apps and games along with specific XR experiences, including the NBA App for Android XR; Nevatars; Fallout: Factions; Project Hail Mary: Journey Among the Stars; the NASCAR XR App; and the San Francisco Ballet Company’s “The Nutcracker.”

Users can opt to plug a computer or handheld gaming console directly into the Xreal Aura via USB-C to make it an augmented display. The device can also allow for various entertainment and productivity use cases by spinning up a multimonitor setup or a big virtual screen.

For audio, the Xreal Aura uses Bose’s tech to power its sound while watching videos or listening to music.

The Xreal Aura is available to order starting today in the United States, Canada, Japan, and South Korea. The 12GB + 256GB version costs $1,279 with a limited launch price of $1,099 through December, and the 16GB + 512GB version is priced at $1,499 with a launch price of $1,299 through December. The company said it will start shipping by mid-November.

In May, Xreal CEO Chi Xu told TechCrunch that building a smart glass business is hard and everyone is losing money . He also said that the Aura glasses will have a wide range of use cases, and the industry has reached an inflection point of having the right hardware, software, and design smart glasses to reach scale.

“You need all the key pieces ready — you need the hardware ready, the operating system needs to be ready, and then you need a great user interface,” Xu said at that time.

items.title: As AI agents reshape the web, Google opens Gemini and Search to more apps
items.summary: A new developer platform will let businesses bring their services to Google's AI experiences, potentially changing how consumers discover and use apps.
items.content:
Google is making it easier for businesses to connect their apps to its AI experiences across Search and Gemini with the debut of its Connected Apps Platform.

Introduced in Gemini and Google Search earlier this year, connected apps let users securely link and interact with popular third-party services, then use them to take specific actions. For instance, you could connect to Canva to design a flyer, or to YouTube Music to build a playlist.

We’ve seen varying takes on the idea by other consumer-facing AI services like ChatGPT and Meta’s Muse. The premise is that such integrations could ultimately shift consumer behavior away from launching and using individual apps to instead using their favorite services through their preferred AI provider.

However, to successfully capture and retain consumers’ attention, there have to actually be a wide range of connected apps to explore.

Google’s idea is to open its doors to any business or developer that wants to reach users through Search or Gemini by allowing them to submit their own connected apps and monitor their performance.

The platform preview is currently available in beta to developers in the U.S., and will allow developers to build and submit apps that can be used across Google’s products.

To get started, developers would integrate with a cloud-hosted MCP (Model Context Protocol) server or Android MCP using the AppFunctions APIs, then use the Google Connected Console to register, test, and submit their app, Google explains.

Essentially, this process lets devs connect their app to Google’s services so it can be used with the search giant’s AI features. Developers can also choose whether they want their app to be available via Search, the Gemini app, or both.

After the app is live, developers can track traffic, latency, and error rates, and maintain control over their brand identity, such as their verified logos and authenticated accounts.

Similar to how SEO allowed companies and websites to show search engine rankings, this could well be one of the initial steps for businesses that want their services to be more visible to users on the agentic web.

Google already has over 50 Connected Apps available in Gemini, including from partners like Adobe, Experian, Localiza, Peloton, and others, in addition to its own expansive set of services, from Workplace and Photos to YouTube Music and Google Home.

These apps will now come to Google Search over the next few weeks. Search today has fewer integrations, featuring apps like Instacart, Canva, YouTube Music, Yahoo Fantasy Football, and others.

Google said meditation app Calm is another new partner on this effort, and that its app will soon launch on both Gemini and Search.

items.title: Chrome’s AI-powered Autofill can now dig through your Gmail to fill out forms
items.summary: The autofill update lets Chrome pull flight confirmations, tracking info, order details, and other information from your inbox, with your permission.
items.content:
Google’s Chrome browser is getting an update that will improve its autofill capabilities using AI. On Wednesday, the company said that Chrome will get an advanced version of autofill that will help users fill out online forms with suggestions pulled from their Gmail.

That means Chrome could suggest things you might need to know, like a flight confirmation number, membership ID, tracking information, order number, address, phone number, or credit card number by referencing your email.

The update is an expansion of Google’s Personal Intelligence, which already allows users to connect their Google Apps to its AI assistant, Gemini, to retrieve certain details and then use them to answer complex questions.

Though seemingly minor, the update could make Chrome easier to use, which could give users another reason to continue to use Google’s browser and stay in its AI ecosystem. It’s reminiscent of one of Apple’s most appreciated features: the ability to automatically detect verification codes sent via text and display them above the keyboard, allowing users to enter them with a single tap.

As with other Personalized Intelligence features, users can decide whether or not to enable enhanced autofill from their Chrome settings. Sensitive data is encrypted, Google notes.

The feature is rolling out to U.S. users on the desktop, and in the iOS and Android apps for Gemini in Chrome.

[깃허브 유니버스 26] 코파일럿 퓨전·프로젝트·오토메이션 공개..."개발부터 검토까지"

컴퓨팅 입력 :2026/10/29 01:10

[샌프란시스코(미국)=김미정 기자] 깃허브가 인공지능(AI) 에이전트로 소프트웨어 개발 전 과정을 지원하는 플랫폼 기능을 확대했다. 작업 계획부터 코드 작성과 검증까지 연결해 개발자가 여러 에이전트에 작업을 맡기고 결과를 검토할 수 있게 돕겠단 전략이다.

깃허브는 28~29일(현지시간) 미국 샌프란시스코에서 열린 연례 개발자 컨퍼런스 '깃허브 유니버스 2026'에서 코파일럿 앱과 퓨전, 프로젝트, 오토메이션 등 신규 제품과 기능을 공개했다. 개발 속도와 품질을 높이고, 작업에 필요한 AI 모델과 도구를 한곳서 활용할 수 있는 생태계를 강화할 방침이다.

이번 발표는 코드 생성량을 늘리는 것뿐 아니라 기능 개발과 오류 수정 등 실제 작업을 완수하는 데 초점 맞췄다. 개발자가 방향을 설정하고 중요한 결정을 내리면 에이전트가 변경 사항을 구현하고 검증하는 것이 골자다. 최종 결과물에 대한 책임은 개발자가 유지한다.

이런 전략 중심에는 '깃허브 코파일럿 앱'이 있다. 이 앱은 여러 프로젝트에서 사용하는 에이전트와 도구를 연결해 개발자가 작업을 일일이 인계하는 부담을 줄인다. 코드 작성뿐 아니라 명세서 작성과 설계 논의 공유, 운영 데이터 분석도 같은 환경에서 수행할 수 있다.

깃허브는 '코파일럿 프로젝트'도 출시했다. 이는 여러 코드 저장 공간에서 에이전트가 동시에 수행하는 작업을 통합 관리한다. 개발자는 한곳에서 진행 상황을 살펴보고 필요한 결정을 내리며 다음 작업을 지시할 수 있다. 개별 작업 실행 과정을 관리하는 부담을 줄이고 개발에 집중하도록 지원한다.

여기서 작업에 사용할 AI 모델은 '코파일럿 퓨전'이 선택, 조율한다. 추론과 코드 생성, 오류 수정 등에 필요한 성능과 비용을 평가해 하나 이상의 모델을 활용하는 실행 방식을 결정한다. 개발자가 작업마다 모델을 직접 고르는 부담을 줄이는 기능이다.

깃허브는 아티피셜 애널리시스 코딩 에이전트 인덱스 평가에서 '퓨전 맥스'가 앤트로픽 '오퍼스 5.5 맥스'와 2점 이내의 점수 차이를 기록했다고 밝혔다. 해당 평가에서 비용은 절반이었으며 작업당 소요 시간은 40% 적었다고 설명했다.

깃허브는 기기나 도구를 바꿔도 같은 작업을 이어가는 '세션 연속성'도 지원한다. 휴대전화에서 에이전트 작업을 시작한 뒤 코드 편집기인 비주얼 스튜디오 코드에서 방향을 조정하고 웹에서 진행 상황을 확인하는 식이다. 개발자가 접속 환경을 바꾸는 동안에도 에이전트는 클라우드에서 작업을 계속한다.

반복 업무 자동화…AI가 작성한 코드 심층 검토

깃허브는 개발 과정 업무 자동화를 위한 '코파일럿 오토메이션'을 내놨다. 이는 개발자가 직접 실행하거나 특정 이벤트가 발생했을 때 또는 정해진 일정에 따라 에이전트가 문제 분류와 우선순위 판단, 코드 검토 등을 수행하도록 설정할 수 있다.

여기에 이전 작업 결과를 바탕으로 개선 방안을 제안하는 기능도 추가됐다. 개발자는 제안 내용을 검토하고 승인할 수 있다. 완료된 작업 기록을 다음 작업 개선에 활용하는 식이다.

깃허브는 코드 품질을 점검하는 '코파일럿 코드 리뷰 맥스'도 공개했다. 깃허브에 따르면 이 기능은 코드 검토 평가인 리뷰벤치에서 심각도 높은 문제를 탐지하는 정확성과 누락 없이 찾아내는 능력을 종합한 에프원 점수에서 가장 높은 점수를 기록한 것으로 나타났다. 일상적인 검토를 빠르게 수행하는 라이트·밸런스드와 달리 변경 사항을 깊이 살펴보는 데 초점을 맞췄다.

새 이용 방식은 깃허브 영업팀을 통해 제공하며, 향후 고객이 직접 신청하는 방식도 지원할 계획이다. 기존 코파일럿 비즈니스와 코파일럿 엔터프라이즈 고객은 현재 요금제를 유지하거나 원하는 시점에 전환할 수 있다.

늘어나는 에이전트에 인프라 확충…"내년 애저 100% 전환 목표"

깃허브는 늘어나는 에이전트 작업을 처리하기 위해 인프라 시설도 확대했다고 밝혔다. 올해 중앙처리장치(CPU) 코어 400만 개와 고속 저장장치 160페타바이트(PB), 초당 50테라비트(Tb) 네트워크 용량을 추가했다.

깃허브는 서비스 운영 환경을 마이크로소프트 애저의 여러 지역에 분산 배치하는 구조로 전환하고 있다. 전환은 내년 초 완료될 예정이다. 코드 버전 관리 기술인 깃(Git) 구조도 기본 구성 요소를 단순화하고 저장장치와 연산 자원을 분리하는 방향으로 개선한다.

제이 파리크 마이크로소프트 코어AI 수석부사장은 "지금까지 작성한 모든 SW는 앞으로 5년간 작성할 SW 1%에도 못 미칠 것"이라며 "이전에는 해결할 수 없었던 문제를 SW로 해결하는 데 있다"고 강조했다.

[깃허브 유니버스 26] '옥토버스 2026' 발표…AI 에이전트, 코드 수정·검토

컴퓨팅 입력 :2026/10/29 01:10

[샌프란시스코(미국)=김미정 기자] 인공지능(AI) 코딩 에이전트가 IT 업계를 넘어 광업과 건설업, 보건의료, 농업 등 산업 전반으로 확산하고 있는 것으로 나타났다. 산업별 현장 문제를 해결하기 위한 AI 개발 프로젝트가 최근 수년간 크게 늘었다는 분석이다.

깃허브가 지난 27일(현지시간) 공개한 '옥토버스 2026' 보고서에 따르면 광업·채석업·석유·가스 채굴업을 지원하는 코드 저장소는 2022년 수치보다 약 65배로 늘어난 것으로 집계됐다. 초기 규모가 작았던 사업지원 서비스업과 건설업은 각각 17~18배 규모로 커졌으며 제조업도 거의 3배 넘게 증가한 것으로 나타났다.

깃허브는 2022년부터 올해까지 생성된 공개 저장소 무작위 표본을 북미산업분류체계에 따라 산업별 AI 에이전트 활용도를 이같이 분석했다. 코드와 관련 자료를 보관하는 저장소 이름과 설명 등을 바탕으로 어떤 산업을 지원하는 프로젝트인지 분류하는 식으로 진행했다.

보고서는 전문·과학·기술 서비스업 관련 저장소는 같은 기간 약 5배 오른 것으로 나타났다. 전체 산업 중 순위도 4위에서 정보산업에 이어 2위로 올라섰다. 농업·임업·어업·수렵업은 두 계단 상승했고 보건의료·사회복지 서비스업도 한 계단 올랐다.

현장 문제를 해결하는 구체적인 개발 사례도 등장했다. 제조업에서는 공구 사진 바탕으로 맞춤형 서랍 정리함을 설계해 3D 프린터로 출력하는 도구가 개발됐다. 보건의료 분야에서는 연구자가 조직 표본 대용량 디지털 이미지를 더 쉽게 분석하도록 돕는 도구도 소개됐다.

대학 연구실은 닭이 뛰놀거나 벌레를 쫓는 행동을 영상으로 분류하는 시스템을 개발한 사례를 발표하기도 했다. 산업 시설에서 재사용할 수 있는 열을 찾아내는 도구도 등장했다. 보고서는 각 분야를 잘 아는 사람들이 AI 코딩 에이전트 도움을 받아 직접 해결책을 구현한 셈이다.

보고서는 산업별 프로젝트 증가가 곧바로 AI 에이전트 활용 확산을 뜻하는 것은 아니라고 선 그었다.

실제 광업과 보건의료·농업 등에서는 저장소 40% 이상이 AI를 언급했지만 에이전트가 제출한 코드 변경 요청이 확인된 저장소는 3%에 그쳤다. 반면 건설업은 AI 언급 비중이 약 25%였으나 에이전트가 코드 변경을 요청한 저장소 비중은 약 9%로 산업 중 가장 높았다.

"AI가 코드 고치고 사람이 검토…개발 방식 바뀐다"

깃허브는 개발자 일하는 방식도 바뀌고 있다고 봤다. 개발자가 AI 에이전트에 작업을 맡기고 결과까지 검토하는 방식이 늘어난 것으로 나타났다.

올해 9월 깃허브에서 제출된 코드 변경 요청인 풀 리퀘스트 40% 이상은 에이전트가 작성한 초안에서 시작됐다. 3월 17%에서 반년 만에 비중이 크게 높아졌다.

9월 한 달간 에이전트가 시작한 코드 변경 요청은 1억 1000만 건으로, 이는 지난 3월보다 약 6배 높은 수치다. 개발자가 원하는 작업을 지시하면 에이전트가 초안을 만들고 사람이 이를 검토하는 방식이 확산한 것이다.

보고서는 작업 전체를 맡기는 기능 이용도 늘었다고 분석했다. 깃허브 코파일럿 월간 활성 사용자 중 에이전트형 기능을 사용하는 비중은 1년 전 35%에서 55%로 상승했다. 작업을 맡기면 독립적으로 수행하는 '코파일럿 클라우드 에이전트' 이용은 전년 대비 230% 증가해 에이전트 채팅 증가율 85%를 웃돌았다.

에이전트가 관여한 코드 변경 요청 가운데 2주 안에 실제 코드에 반영된 비중은 2월 83%에서 9월 90%로 높아졌다. 에이전트 관여가 감지되지 않은 요청은 두 시점 모두 약 86%였다.

검토와 보안 도구 이용도 늘어난 것으로 분석됐다. AI 지원 코드 검토와 깃허브 어드밴스트 시큐리티 이용량은 각각 전년 대비 90% 이상 증가했다. 코드에 포함된 API 키와 비밀번호 등 노출을 탐지하는 푸시 보호 기능은 올해 58억 회 검사를 수행했다.

깃허브는 전체 개발 활동도 사상 최대 규모로 늘었다고 봤다. 지난해 10월부터 올해 9월까지 개발자들이 코드 변경 사항을 깃허브에 전송한 횟수는 179억 회였다. 이는 2024년과 2025년을 합친 것보다 큰 규모다.

특히 코드 변경 이력을 저장하는 커밋은 공개·비공개 저장소를 합쳐 343억 회로 집계됐다. 이는 2년 전 3배가 넘는 규모다. 실제 코드에 반영된 변경 요청도 같은 기간 3배 이상 늘어 13억 건에 달한 것으로 나타났다.

올해 생성된 저장소 중 에이전트 설정 파일이 있는 저장소 평균 커밋 수는 해당 파일이 없는 신규 저장소보다 8배 더 높았다. 이 파일은 에이전트 작동 방식과 작업 방향을 설정하는 데 쓰인다. 다만 커밋 수는 코드 변경 활동량을 나타내는 지표로 생산성이나 소프트웨어 품질이 8배 높다는 의미는 아닌 것으로 확인됐다.

현재 깃허브를 이용하는 전 세계 개발자는 2억 2500만 명을 넘어섰다. 미국과 인도가 각각 3830만 명과 3200만 명으로 가장 많은 비중을 차지했다. 두 나라 모두 올해 개발자가 1000만 명 이상 늘었다. 공개 저장소에서 이뤄진 기여 활동도 25억 회로 지난해 11억 2000만 회보다 두 배 많다.

AI 모델도 골라 쓴다…복잡한 계획과 간단한 작업 나눠 활용

개발자들은 AI 모델 하나에 의존하기보다 작업에 맞춰 여러 모델을 사용한 것으로 나타났다.

보고서는 9 월 모델을 직접 선택한 깃허브 코파일럿 사용자 중 61%는 두 개 이상 모델을 이용했다고 밝혔다. 4개월 전에는 50%였다.

유료 사용자가 이용한 모델 종류는 5월 29종에서 9월 47종으로 늘었다. 9월에는 어떤 단일 모델도 전체 요청의 25%를 넘게 차지하지 않았다.

개발자가 모델을 직접 선택한 요청 100건 중 범용 모델은 38건을 차지했다. 복잡한 추론과 계획에 초점을 맞춘 모델은 37건이었고 빠르고 가벼운 모델은 25건이었다. 개발자들이 필요한 기능과 속도·비용에 따라 모델을 나눠 쓰는 모습이다.

모델 선택 자체를 코파일럿에 맡기는 이용자도 늘었다. 유료 깃허브 코파일럿 사용자 중 63%는 9월에 자동 모델 선택 기능을 한 번 이상 사용했다. 깃허브는 작업 단계별로 모델을 배정하는 기능을 자동 선택과 결합한 '깃허브 코파일럿 퓨전'도 정식 제공한다고 밝혔다.

깃허브는 "문득 떠올린 아이디어를 실제로 작동하는 무언가로 만드는 일이 훨씬 쉬워졌다"며 "무엇을 만들지, 누구를 위해 만들지는 여전히 개발자에 달렸다"고 밝혔다.

items.title: GitHub Universe 2026: Evolving every layer of the stack
items.summary: Today, we laid out our vision for GitHub as the most comprehensive, end-to-end software delivery system in the world. The post GitHub Universe 2026: Evolving every layer of the stack appeared first on The GitHub Blog .
items.content:
Our jobs as developers are changing. In a couple of years, we’ve gone from writing every line of code to working with AI assistants to orchestrating fleets of agents. But the goal hasn’t changed: ship completed software work. A feature, a bug fix, a security fix. Completed work, not more code, is the output that matters.

Today at GitHub Universe , we shared our vision for GitHub as the most comprehensive software delivery system in the world. We introduced products that bring that vision to life and showed how we’re rebuilding the infrastructure underneath it.

The SDLC is no longer a linear path from planning to coding to testing to deployment. A code change, a request from a colleague, or a production metric can trigger work anywhere in the system. Most of us (and our agents) jump between different stages, depending on the task at hand. Developers set the direction, make decisions, and stay accountable for what ships. Agents implement and verify changes. And everything feeds into and out of a continuous learning machine that makes the next cycle better.

This agentic software delivery system solves for three things:

GitHub is built for developers and their agents. We’re also making the underlying primitives available, so you can build your own bespoke solutions. You stay in control of the work, the tools, and the cost.

Today at Universe, we showed some of the latest products and features in action, starting with the GitHub Copilot app.

The GitHub Copilot app is designed from the ground up for agentic software delivery. It connects your agents and tools across projects, so you can direct the work without making every handoff. And it’s for more than producing code: you can write specs, present design discussions, or analyze telemetry in one agent-first surface.

Different tasks need different models. Developers shouldn’t have to manage every model choice to get the right result at the right price. Copilot Fusion evaluates what a task needs across reasoning, code generation, debugging, and tool use, then chooses how to execute across one or more models. In the Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index, Fusion Max scored within two points of Opus 5.5 Max at half the cost and 40% less time per task.

Available natively in the GitHub Copilot app starting today, Copilot projects let you run agent work across multiple repos in fully managed, parallel sessions. You have one place to track progress, make decisions, and direct what happens next. That means you can spend less time managing execution and more time deciding what’s worth building.

Your work shouldn’t restart when you switch devices or tools. Session continuity lets you start and follow the same cloud agent session across the GitHub app, VS Code, the CLI, and the web. Start from your phone at standup, steer it from VS Code at your desk, and check in on it from github.com at lunch. The agent keeps working in the cloud. Our multi-model harness that enables it is powerful, fast, and cost-efficient.

Copilot automations let you create AI-powered workflows within your repo. They run in the cloud, and you can kick them off manually or set them up to respond to an event or run on a schedule. That lets you coordinate agents to handle tasks such as issue triage and code review. And now, automations can learn from their outcomes and propose improvements for you to review and approve. That’s the learning engine in practice. Use the results of the completed work to make the next run better.

More code means more pull requests and more demand for review. Moving faster only helps if we can maintain the quality of what ships. Copilot code review surfaces meaningful, actionable bugs that developers need to catch. Today, we introduced Copilot code review Max, which posted the highest F1 score on ReviewBench for high-severity issues. Lite and Balanced keep everyday reviews fast; the new Max provides a deeper look when a change needs it.

Starting today, GitHub Enterprise customers can use all Copilot features without buying a separate subscription. That includes GitHub Copilot app, code review, automations, and more. You pay for the AI credits you use.

This is available through GitHub Sales today, with self-serve coming soon. Existing Copilot Business and Copilot Enterprise customers can keep their current plans or move over when they’re ready. GitHub also remains open and extensible. Keep using the tools your team depends on, including Cloudflare, Datadog, Figma, and more.

All of this depends on a foundation that’s fast, reliable, and built to scale. Agents are changing the volume and shape of software development. Adding capacity matters, but capacity alone won’t get us there. We’ve also had to change the architecture.

So far this year, we’ve added:

We’re also migrating to a multi-region deployment in Azure , while continuing to serve incredible levels of traffic from developers around the world. We expect to complete the migration early next year. Those investments give us more room to grow. The next step is building the systems that handle the work.

We’ve scaled Git for years as activity on GitHub has grown. The agentic era calls for a different ceiling on throughput and reliability. Three principles guide our new Git architecture : simplify the primitives, decouple storage from compute, and minimize coordination.

Git’s just one example of the work we’re doing to scale the platform. We’ve done a lot of work across GitHub’s AI gateway, the harness, and much more.

Our jobs are changing, but developers are more important than ever. I think all the software we’ve written to date will amount to less than 1% of the software we’ll write in the next five years. The opportunity isn’t just to produce more code. It’s to solve problems we couldn’t solve before.

items.title: Octoverse: Commits, pushes, reach new highs in 2026 as developers build with agents
items.summary: See how a record year of growth reached every industry, every field, and every kind of builder in the 2026 Octoverse report. The post Octoverse: Commits, pushes, reach new highs in 2026 as developers build with agents appeared first on The GitHub Blog .
items.content:
Developers pushed code to GitHub 17.9 billion times in the past 12 months, more than in 2024 and 2025 combined.

Behind that number are developers building what interests them and what their communities need. In Nepal, one developer built a flood bulletin on GitHub Pages with verified information on roads, rescue, weather, and power. It has since grown into Gati , a Nepali-first relay of official disaster alerts that runs on GitHub Pages and Actions. Elsewhere, developers at NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory are creating software designed to run programs aboard spacecraft , and fans built open-source firmware that lets people customize their e-readers . Curiosity, aimed in every direction, at a scale GitHub hasn’t seen before.

That growth happened quickly. Partway through the year, activity on GitHub bent sharply upward, just as agents went from something developers were trying out to something they were working alongside. Developers picked from more models than ever and built in industries we are highlighting in this report for the first time, from health care to agriculture.

Octoverse is our chance to step back and look at the whole picture. This year, that picture is bigger than ever. Here is what stood out most:

Underneath it all, AI models and the harnesses built around them have advanced over the past year, and developers have more to choose from. Growth is moving quickly: one year into last year’s five-year developer growth projections, every country we projected has already closed at least a fifth of its distance to 2030, and our own forecasting models no longer agree on where it will go next.

This year was all about momentum. Developers pushed code changes to GitHub 17.9 billion times in the past 12 months, more than 2024 and 2025 combined. Commits across all repo types (public and private) climbed even faster to 34.3 billion, more than three times where they stood two years ago. Merged pull requests more than tripled to 1.3 billion over the same period, an average of 3.5 million a day.

Agents were one of the tools developers leaned on hardest this year, pulling them deeper into daily work. Among repos created this year, the average repo with an agent configuration file logged eight times as many commits as the average new repo without one, sign that individuals and teams building with agents from day one are moving at a markedly different pace.

Developers also relied on automations to keep projects moving. GitHub Actions ran a job 1,440 times every second this year. This equals 124 million times a day and is more than three times last year’s total. Developers merged more than 30 million Dependabot pull requests to keep dependencies current and reduce the use of known vulnerabilities, about double 2025’s pace.

Our telemetry shows activity climbing steadily from January, then surging around June, as if developers everywhere saw new possibilities at once. Right around then, a cluster of industry-wide shifts landed: better underlying models, the harnesses and tools built around them, and the agents running on both. Agents moved from single-session tools to persistent ones that could track progress across days and orchestrate other specialized agents. Just as important, agents began making extensive use of the cloud, executing work remotely as well as on local machines.

This momentum is showing up both in brand-new repos and from developers who have been building for years. From June onwards, about 55% of all commits came from brand new repositories. But plenty more commits came from developers who’ve been around a while: developers who pushed code in the past 12 months have been on GitHub for an average of 36 months, and of those who opened a pull request in August, more than 75% pushed code in September. They are also branching out: the average developer now works across 10% more repositories than they did a year ago.

That staying power shows up in open source too. Public contributions soared to 2.5 billion in 2026, more than double last year’s total (1.12 billion). Behind those numbers are developers who keep showing up, like @kinlane, who made more than 1 million contributions across his public repositories using agentic workflows to keep a machine-readable catalog of public API information current. Another example is @kim-em , who made more than 178,000 contributions while maintaining mathlib, which is a community library of computer-checked mathematics. @andig , a maintainer of the open source EV charging controller and home energy management system evcc , contributed over 21,000 times.

These are just a few examples of the work millions of developers do every day. To all the developers doing work like this and beyond: we see you, and we’re glad you’re building.

Behind every number in this report is a developer. GitHub now serves more than 225 million of them, and the community is growing around the globe. The United States (38.3 million) and India (32 million) remain the two largest developer communities, and each added more than 10 million developers this year. Brazil added 3.28 million developers on GitHub this year, the third most of any country.

Last year, we projected that India would reach 57.5 million developers by 2030 and the United States 54.7 million. One year into that five-year window, every country in our projections has already closed at least a fifth of the distance to its own 2030 figure. The United States has closed 38.6%, and India 28.3%.

The same momentum shows up across regions, each with its own local context:
